body:
Here are the details on how Donald Trump -- while in Florida -- voted by mail and played golf instead of voting in-person ahead of a 2026 special election, straight from Politico:
" Trump requested his mail-in ballot on Saturday, March 14, according to public Palm Beach County voter records. The ballot was sent to Trump’s Mar-a-Lago estate the same day and was received for processing the next day, on Sunday, March 15.
T he president was in Palm Beach both days, at his golf club from 8:45 a.m. to 2:37 p.m. on Saturday, and 9:21 a.m. to 1:55 p.m. on Sunday, according to press pool reports. In-person early voting was open from Saturday, March 14 through Sunday, March 22 at 7 p.m. "
Listen, we hate asking for money in every email. Unlike opponents of voting rights, however, there are no secret wealthy donors backing our efforts. There are just our supporters, kicking in $5, $15, or $35 whenever they can. Please chip in today if you can and help us defend our fundamental right to vote >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=042826_4&amount=35]
Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
AP: Trump casts Florida mail ballot as he pushes Congress to severely limit that voting option [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=042826_4&amount=25]
Team: Donald Trump voted by mail. No, we're not referring to his well-documented past usage of the practice.
No, after years of attacking vote-by-mail, countless late-night Truth Social rants, and several executive orders within the last year trying to end, or at least curtail, mail-in voting, Donald Trump voted by mail this week, in a Florida special election held on March 24, 2026 . He could have gone to an early voting site when he was at Mar-A-Lago the week before the election, but he chose to submit a mailed ballot instead, according to Palm Beach County voter records.
To be honest, we here at Voter Action Project are glad he did. We believe every eligible American deserves to vote in the manner that is easiest for them to participate. That's because we believe that the act of participation is the most important part, not what method you use to cast your ballot.
It's worth noting, however, how he's very willing to use this tool to help himself and make his own voice heard, but he wants to restrict it for everyone else if it seems like it might not benefit him. The pattern is completely clear, and his self-interest drives every decision and statement he makes about voting.
So next time you run into that anti-voting family member, friend, or neighbor, just let them know: Trump himself chose to skip voting in person while in Florida and voted by mail in 2026.
Onward,
The Voter Action Project Team

name: Chris Pappas
subject: $17 million is a big number
body:
[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/126?t=1001&akid=6375%2E582294%2EWJskfQ ]Chris Pappas for Senate[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/126?t=1002&akid=6375%2E582294%2EWJskfQ ]Chris Pappas for Senate

The top Republican Senate super PAC plans to spend $17 million in New
Hampshire to boost my opponent John Sununu.

Here’s what this means: Very soon there won’t be a quiet moment left on
Granite Staters’ airwaves. Whether you’re catching the local news, sitting
down for a Hulu binge after work, or just watching YouTube with your kids,
these pro-Sununu ads will be inescapable.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260428_2.3OKLNo&refcode=em20260428-2&t=1003&akid=6375%2E582294%2EWJskfQ ]I’ll need the help of this grassroots team to fight back. Can you chip
in $5 or any amount so we can stay competitive with this
onslaught of super PAC spending?

$17 million is a big number — and it’s the largest investment national
Republicans have made in our state in a decade.

You don’t see that kind of spending here unless they think they have a
real shot at flipping this seat.

And with this race, they do.

This will be the first open U.S. Senate race in New Hampshire in sixteen
years. Open seats are different. They draw more attention, more outside
money, and more pressure from national groups looking for an opportunity
to put their finger on the scale.

Republicans haven’t won a Senate race here since 2010 — the last time
there was an open seat. They see this as their best chance in years to
change that – and they’re investing accordingly.

But what’s happening here isn’t just about one seat.

The Senate majority could come down to a handful of states, and keeping
New Hampshire blue is the only way Democrats have a chance at flipping it.
With the MAGA movement shaping the direction of the GOP, that control
carries real consequences.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260428_2.3OKLNo&refcode=em20260428-2&t=1004&akid=6375%2E582294%2EWJskfQ ]There’s a lot at stake — and this is our chance to prove that Granite
Staters still value our independence and that New Hampshire is not for
sale. Will you chip in today to help keep New Hampshire blue?

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260428_2.3OKLNo&amount=5&refcode=em20260428-2&t=1023&akid=6375%2E582294%2EWJskfQ ]Donate $5 »

Thank you,

Chris

clean_body: | | | Peter, ... I promise, I wouldn’t normally message you, but this couldn’t wait a second longer. My name is Natalie Dolezal, and for the last 18 years, I’ve been blessed to be Greg’s wife and the mother of our four beautiful children — Naomi, Lincoln, Norah, and Neeva. Our home in Forsyth County is filled with faith, laughter, bedtime prayers, and the everyday joy of raising a family. Greg has always been our steady rock — the dad who makes time to be there for our kids’ games and activities, lead family devotions, and show them what it means to love God and serve others. But I’ve also watched him make real sacrifices for something bigger. The long nights at the Capitol, the missed dinners, the weekends away fighting for families across Georgia. Greg’s the kind of man who couldn’t sit still while our daughters’ sports and locker rooms were under threat – so he authored and passed the Riley Gaines Act to keep men out of women’s sports and protect girls across our state. Greg saw parents losing control of their children’s education — so he championed the Georgia Promise Scholarship to give every kid a real chance, no matter their ZIP code. And when it mattered most, Greg stood strong with President Trump, defending election integrity and fighting for the values that make America great. I’ve seen the late nights, the tough fights, and the quiet moments when he comes home exhausted but never defeated —because he knows he’s fighting for our kids and yours. I’ve stood by my husband for 18 years... ...I’ve seen every sacrifice and every good he’s done for families across Georgia. Now, with so much at stake in this race for Lieutenant Governor, my question to you is urgent: ? If you don’t step up right now, the Radical Left will keep coming after everything we hold dear... ...Our daughters’ sports, our parental rights, our secure elections, and the safe, free future our children deserve. We risk losing the ground we’ve fought so hard to protect without strong leaders like my husband leading the way. Greg is ready to fight harder than ever in the Lt. Governor’s office, but he needs you in his corner ASAP. This fight won’t wait. body:
Two manufactured attacks in one week
# [](https://francescahong.com?refcode=em20260428-2765)
Peter,
The attacks on Fran are getting weirder — and that means we’re winning.
[Last week](https://act.francescahong.com/go/11538?t=1&akid=2765%2E105371%2EOlApqJ), Republican operatives — including a Trump advisor — accused her of wearing a “satanic” hat. The “666” they spotted? Three Gs her son George scribbled on her hat with a marker when he was first learning to write his name.
[](https://act.francescahong.com/go/11538?t=2&akid=2765%2E105371%2EOlApqJ)
A few days later, they dug up a $25 donation Fran made in 2020 to a Democratic Assembly candidate running against a Republican incumbent. Why now? Because that former candidate posted something awful online last week — and the right-wing media decided Fran should answer for it, five years later. The post was idiotic, and so was the attack.
It’s a classic tactic. Manufacture outrage. Force the candidate to respond. Waste everyone’s time. Repeat.
We’re not playing.
Here’s what’s actually happening:
* Fran is still leading the Democratic primary and growing her supporter base every day.
* Our volunteer team has grown to over 3,000 strong! No other candidate else has this much enthusiasm around their campaign.
* We’re showing up in every corner of the state to collect signatures and get on the ballot.
* And we’re doing it without a dime of corporate PAC money.

We have the broadest base. We have the best policies. And we have the most momentum behind us — which is exactly why they’re throwing everything they’ve got (and what they’ve got, frankly, is weak sauce.)
Let them keep attacking hats and digging in the trash heap of history. We’ll keep fighting for permanent affordability for working people in Wisconsin.
**[So tonight, instead of $2 Tuesday, we’re making it $25 Tuesday.](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260428.vU0oQc&refcode=em20260428-2765&t=3&akid=2765%2E105371%2EOlApqJ)**

With gratitude,
Team Hong

### 🐾 WOOF! Bailey the campaign dog here with an important update from Team Haley HQ.
Apr 29
---

---

---

---

**WOOF WOOF!! It 's me! Bailey, the official campaign dog for Haley Stevens! 🐶💙**
I'm a certified good girl, treat enthusiast, floor-based napper, and proud emotional support animal for the entire Team Haley pack. 🦴✨
My mom, Katelyn, is Haley Stevens' finance director, and I'm barking at you with an update, because my mom and the human people are being ... how do I put this ... suuuper intense.
There are SO many laptops. Coffee cups. Spreadsheets. They keep saying things like "end-of-month numbers" and "two-day window" and "close the fundraising gap."
And I'm like, wow. Y'all. The vibes are intense.
Everybody needs a walk. Maybe we all nap for 12 to 14 hours a day? Maybe we get new chew toys? Or embrace the healing power of finding a recently dropped Coney dog?
But apparently, the humans are saying this is a very important time!!!
**[Because Team Haley has an end-of-month deadline in two days, and they're trying to hit a goal of $200,000 to keep this campaign's momentum going strong.](https://substack.com/redirect/8d61dd0a-5752-46b7-bb1d-3cbc0f729677?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
And yes, I know what you're thinking: "Bailey, for real for real, how much do you actually understand about campaign finance?"
To which I say: Not much!! I'm a dog!! I literally eat food off the floor!! 🐾
But I _do_ know a few things: **I know Michigan is a doggone HUGE race, and Senate control could be decided here.**
I know the polls are looking good for Haley - I keep hearing the humans say things like, "She's the strongest Democrat in the race" and all that stuff. And I know that when Team Haley starts moving around fast and typing loud, the stakes are real.
I also know this: Michiganders are PAWESOME, and Haley works her tail off for them.
**Honestly, her hustle makes me tired, and I have twice as many legs!**
The doggone truth is that Haley loves Michigan more than I love a dropped slice of Buddy's pizza. And humans, let me just say, you know I'm a dog, and I do not know how to lie: **THAT IS LOVE. 🍕👀**
And from where I'm laying - usually under my mom's desk - I can tell this campaign has real momentum. Judging purely by the number of pets I've gotten at campaign events, I'd say this campaign has a lot of people excited for Haley to get to work in the Senate!

subject: Enough is enough—an update from Reagan Dunn.

body:
You deserve accountability. Help me demand it. | | https://us5.forward-to-friend.com/forward?u=0220f14f6bfeefc23687abe64&id;=6de8808441&e;=77eef70c61 | Is this email not displaying correctly?

| | Friend,

I am reaching out to you with an important update about your taxpayer dollars.
* **Recently** , [a series of reports and investigations](https://reagandunn.us5.list-manage.com/track/click?u=0220f14f6bfeefc23687abe64&id=1a08120144&e=77eef70c61) have confirmed serious problems with how public dollars were managed. These investigations stem from my work to demand an Audit of King County DCHS funding years ago.
* **Then** , a joint report by the County Auditor and Ombuds outlined significant financial risks and made recommendations to strengthen King County's financial security.
* **Now** , a forensic review of the King County Regional Homelessness Authority (KCRHA) has uncovered significant financial mismanagement of taxpayer dollars.

_**You deserve accountability. [Help me demand it!](https://reagandunn.us5.list-manage.com/track/click?u=0220f14f6bfeefc23687abe64&id=d23f3371aa&e=77eef70c61)**_
Friend, as unacceptable as these findings are, they are unfortunately not a bit surprising. I first pointed out the failures of the KCRHA model all the way back in 2019, and [wrote an Op-Ed](https://reagandunn.us5.list-manage.com/track/click?u=0220f14f6bfeefc23687abe64&id=2f5b3df65b&e=77eef70c61) in the Seattle Times calling for King County to separate from the failed system years ago.

_Enough is enough._ That's why I've been leading the charge for real reforms to solve each of the problems mentioned above.
* **Recently** , the King County Council unanimously passed my legislation to reform our grant funding processes.
* **Then** , I co-sponsored legislation to create an independent Inspector General Division with the authority to investigate fraud, recover misspent dollars, and finally bring real accountability to county government.
* **Now** , I'm working to pass legislation to pull King County out of the disastrous KCRHA entirely.

This is my focus: identifying waste, demanding accountability, and making sure government actually delivers results for the people paying for it (YOU).

But I can't do this work alone. _I need your help._**Would you be willing to[make a one-time contribution of $25, $35, or even $75](https://reagandunn.us5.list-manage.com/track/click?u=0220f14f6bfeefc23687abe64&id=6464eac18a&e=77eef70c61) to help me ****_amplify the message_** that taxpayer dollars need to be protected from waste, misuse, and abuse? \--------------------
**[DONATE NOW](https://reagandunn.us5.list-manage.com/track/click?u=0220f14f6bfeefc23687abe64&id=616fe57d52&e=77eef70c61)**
\-------------------- Friend, your support over the years has meant the world to me, and you inspire me to keep fighting for you!

Thank you!
Reagan Dunn

| Hi friend, Juan here–

We've been putting in work for our Veterans, and I am excited to share the latest updates!

Serving those who served our country is not optional. It’s a responsibility. Here in AZ-06, we take that responsibility seriously. **Our district is home to over 80,000 Veterans,_ranking 9th in the nation in Veteran population._**

These are our neighbors and friends, and they deserve to be heard after all of their sacrifices to our country.

And that’s exactly what we’ve been focused on delivering.

Since taking office, we’ve helped return **OVER $4 MILLION** directly to Veterans and their families through casework. But we know benefits are useless without access and support. That’s why we’re working to **[expand care for rural Veterans](https://juanciscomani.us6.list-manage.com/track/click?u=4ed32a393c9fe1089f10fee94&id=9228e04896&e=659fba240e),** making sure distance doesn’t stand in the way of getting the help they’ve earned. And we’re continuing to push for more awareness and resources around _**mental health and suicide prevention**_ for our service members, because no Veteran should ever feel like they’re facing that battle alone.
---
|
---
---
|
---
| **LEGISLATION THAT DELIVERS**** ** 🇺🇸 We’ve backed that commitment up with action, working on all of the following bills to support our Veterans ✅ **Prioritizing Veterans’ Survivors Act (H.R. 1228)**
Making sure families of Veterans get the benefits they were promised and a direct line to the VA when they need help most. ✅ **Veterans Readiness & Employment Program Integrity Act (H.R. 3579)**
Improving accountability and outcomes in job training programs so Veterans can transition successfully into the workforce. ✅ **Rural Veterans Improved Access to Benefits Act (H.R. 3951)**
Expanding access to disability exams so rural Veterans can get care faster. ✅ **VETS Opportunity Act (H.R. 1458)**
Modernizing the GI Bill and expanding education options for Veterans, Guard, and Reserve members.

We ask a lot of our service members and their families. The least we can do is to make sure they are supported when they come home. Helping them transition back into civilian life, find jobs, get an education, and ensure they have access to the mental and physical care that they need.
---
|
---
|
---
| **THANK YOU** to all of our Veterans in AZ-06! It is an honor to serve you.

See you around the district!

– Juan

And we’re continuing to push for more awareness and resources around mental health and suicide prevention for our service members, because no Veteran should ever feel like they’re facing that battle alone. | | | LEGISLATION THAT DELIVERS 🇺🇸 We’ve backed that commitment up with action, working on all of the following bills to support our Veterans ✅ Prioritizing Veterans’ Survivors Act (H.R. 1228) Making sure families of Veterans get the benefits they were promised and a direct line to the VA when they need help most. ✅ Veterans Readiness & Employment Program Integrity Act (H.R. 3579) Improving accountability and outcomes in job training programs so Veterans can transition successfully into the workforce. ✅ Rural Veterans Improved Access to Benefits Act (H.R. 3951) Expanding access to disability exams so rural Veterans can get care faster. ✅ VETS Opportunity Act (H.R. 1458) Modernizing the GI Bill and expanding education options for Veterans, Guard, and Reserve members. We ask a lot of our service members and their families. The least we can do is to make sure they are supported when they come home. Helping them transition back into civilian life, find jobs, get an education, and ensure they have access to the mental and physical care that they need. | | | THANK YOU to all of our Veterans in AZ-06! It is an honor to serve you. See you around the district! – Juan | "JOIN ME IN DEFENDING AZ-06" | | | PAID FOR BY CISCOMANI FOR CONGRESS | | | | | Copyright © 2026 Ciscomani for Congress, All rights reserved.

subject: I wanted to step in here real quick to share how hard Gina is working right now
body:

Hi Peter, it’s Gina’s husband, John.
Before I say anything, I just want to say how proud I am of Gina and how grateful I am for this team. The volunteers, the supporters, the people showing up every day, the grassroots supporters — _all of you make this possible._
Right now, I’m stepping in for a moment because Gina and her team are on the phones right now, pushing hard to hit our **$100,000 fundraising goal.**
[**If you can, will you chip in $5 right now to help the team close the gap and hit their fundraising goal by Thursday?**](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260428_3_john.hzoPcH&refcode=em20260428-1017&amount=5&t=1&akid=1017%2E299639%2EfaS4vS)
Gina is working day in and day out on this campaign, but she’s not slowing down. She’s been traveling across Texas and talking with families about what their issues are and what they deserve from their next governor.
She’s not running to climb the political ladder, Peter, she’s running because she believes Texas should work for the people who live here — not the billionaires and special interests who have bought their way into Texas through the way of Greg Abbott’s office.
I’ve watched Gina spend years showing up for Texans, defending public schools, standing up for working families, and taking on corruption in Austin. _That is who she is._ And I know there is no better person to replace Greg Abbott after this fall.
And right now, we need the resources to make sure voters hear directly from Gina in these critical months leading up to the election.
**[So, can I count on you to make a donation of $5 before Gina’s fundraising deadline on April 30?](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260428_3_john.hzoPcH&refcode=em20260428-1017&amount=5&t=2&akid=1017%2E299639%2EfaS4vS)**

Thank you for your support. It means a lot to Gina, so it means a lot to me, too.
With gratitude,
John Donisi

[1]Justice Democrats

Peter,

Justice Democrats-endorsed candidate Melat Kiros is making waves and
shaking up the political establishment in Denver:

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260428-mk.2HQAYk&refcode=em20260428-37721&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1002&akid=37721%2E1203867%2E7qQgdq ]Headline from The Denver Post;'A young Democrat stunned Rep. Diana
DeGette in a party vote. Against the odds, Melat Kiros is gunning for a
primary win: In challnge of veteran congresswoman, 28-year-old says
'Denver Democrats want a fighter''

Melat surged to prominence after defeating 30-year incumbent Rep. Diana
DeGette at the Denver County Democratic Assembly — earning 63% of the vote
and handing Degette her first assembly loss since 1996.

While the assembly doesn’t decide the primary, moments like this don’t
happen by accident. They point to something real: momentum.

A growing number of voters are looking for a different kind of Democrat —
one who’s willing to challenge the status quo and actually fight for
transformative change.

Melat is running to do exactly that. [ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260428-mk.2HQAYk&refcode=em20260428-37721&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1003&akid=37721%2E1203867%2E7qQgdq ]Help her win with a grassroots
donation now!

She said it herself: “We hear politicians say over and over that we need
bold leadership, progress, and change. We’ve heard this for years.
Decades. But they never deliver.”

She’s running to change that, fueled by the story that got her here.

Melat was born in Ethiopia and raised in Denver after immigrating with her
family as a baby. After college and law school, she was on her way to
build a career as an attorney.

But after speaking out against Israel’s genocide against Palestinians and
law firms’ targeting pro-Palesinian protesters, Melat lost her job — a
turning point that pushed her towards public service and a deeper
commitment to reforming a political system she believes isn’t working for
everyday people.

Today, when she’s not on the campaign trail, she works as a barista, so
she knows firsthand what it’s like to be a service industry worker at a
time when working-class folks are struggling to get by as corporate
profits soar.

Melat’s campaign is centered on bold, structural change, focusing on:

* Medicate for All;
* Universal childcare;
* Publicly financed elections to reduce the influence of big money.

And she’s prepared to hold her own party accountable to deliver, which is
exactly why Justice Democrats is proud to support her.

But taking on a longtime incumbent backed by the establishment means Melat
needs a surge of grassroots support to keep building on her momentum and
stay competitive. That’s where you come in,
Peter.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260428-mk.2HQAYk&refcode=em20260428-37721&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1004&akid=37721%2E1203867%2E7qQgdq ]Will you split a contribution to Justice Democrats and Melat’s campaign
before Thursday’s fundraising deadline? Every dollar will help us continue
organizing, reaching voters, and amplifying her message ahead of the
primary.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260428-mk.2HQAYk&refcode=em20260428-37721&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1023&akid=37721%2E1203867%2E7qQgdq ]Contribute $5

Melat has proven she can build momentum — it’s up to all of us to help her
sustain it.

In solidarity,

Justice Democrats

Peter, I just got off the stage after the second debate in this race for governor, and I want to tell you exactly what happened.
This race is coming down to a simple question: _who is actually fighting for Californians, and who is trying to buy their way into power?_
Californians are getting squeezed from every direction—rent that eats half a paycheck, child care that costs more than a mortgage, and wages that just don’t keep up.
**People need solutions, and they deserve to know who’s trying to buy influence in this race.**
Tom Steyer has now poured over $144 million of his own money into his campaign. Others are backed by Big Oil and corporate interests that keep costs high for working families across California.
And the Republicans in this race are still pushing Donald Trump’s MAGA agenda—decimating our rights, denying climate science, and doubling down on the same failed policies that hurt everyday Californians.
I’ve built my career on calling this out clearly, directly, and with receipts. When I bring a whiteboard, it’s because people deserve to see exactly who is funding what, and who benefits.
**As governor, I’ll do the same.**
I don’t take corporate PAC money, I’m not self-funding this campaign, and I’m not here to protect the status quo. I’m here to change it.
**The primary is coming fast, and only the top two candidates move on to November. What we do right now will decide whether we have a real chance to win this race and deliver for working families.**

Thursday at midnight is our end-of-month deadline. That's 2 days from now.
I want to be clear about why this deadline matters and what we're building toward.
Every dollar we raise before Thursday determines our May budget. That budget funds the infrastructure we need to flip VA-05:
Digital ads introducing me to voters across the newly drawn district who don't know me yet. We need to reach thousands of voters who just learned they're in the 5th District because of redistricting.
Field organizers knocking doors and having real conversations with voters. VA-05 covers a lot of ground, and we need people on the ground in every community building support.
Voter contact infrastructure — phone banks, text programs, and volunteer coordination — to reach persuadable voters and turn out our base in November.
Campaign literature we can distribute at events, leave at doors, and mail to key precincts.
This is how we build a campaign that can compete and win. But only if we hit our goals.

body:

_**A Special Message from our Sponsor**_ _Please note that views expressed in this message do not necessarily reflect those of_ _Parler_ _and do not constitute an endorsement or recommendation by_ _Parler_ _._
---
| Jim Jordan \- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - | | Friend,
---
I’m not writing you this letter from _Congressman_ Jim Jordan.
---
Instead, I’m writing to you just as _Jim_ – husband, father of 4, and sports fan.
---
So, as a fellow patriot like you who loves our country, I say this with a heavy heart...
---
... _A far-Left Democrat Governor just RIGGED the congressional map in Virginia, likely costing Republicans 4 SEATS in the House_.
---
In response, some have turned to despair: _“It’s all over.” “We’re doomed.” “We’re powerless.”_
---
Some have even blamed top activists like you for the loss for not giving an extra donation on a random Tuesday. _They are just shameful for saying that..._
---
Let’s be honest. That’s _not_ the American spirit.
---
**Does that doom and gloom sound like President Trump when he was targeted...wrongfully ARRESTED FOUR TIMES...and still kept fighting?**
---
Here’s the truth: _I don’t care if the polling says we’re down 99 points and a storm is brewing, you will _NEVER_ hear the word “SURRENDER” come out of my mouth._
---
That’s a promise.
---
And I’ve put skin in the game to prove it... I’ve been _SUED_ _and_ _SPIED_ on by the Deep State – and all because they know I fight for YOU.
---
**Now comes our most important fight. We can’t let the Democrats get away with rigging the congressional map.**
---
Emergency mid-decade redistricting battles are now taking place all across America – and with ZERO margin for error, we need to know exactly who will show up to vote.
---
That means our Trump Voter Census has to be 100% complete and 100% accurate – and I know with absolute confidence that the President and I can count on you. _Now let’s make it official._
---
[**So please, complete the brief questionnaire to verify YOUR profile in our Census now that a nationwide redistricting battle is looming.**](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ4NjF9AAwAAAAAAFUCUGKaob1bMLMnpkEjUuR0mZniMN7_VPD6F_FRGnc2J6BzcXKOdOre9gxFNYHpWTYy-kKmjmxtKA1tI0AfpVdqATmVn0VlygKEh_Ufxw)

---

Thank you, God bless you, and NEVER, EVER GIVE UP!

body:
That decision shaped decades of failed treatments.

For years, RFK was mocked as a conspiracy theorist.
Then he was right...
About the lab leak.
About microplastics.
About the FDA.
Now he’s warning Americans again.
This time, it affects millions... especially anyone born before January 1st, 1969.
It involves a hearing health issue most doctors dismiss and tell patients to live with. RFK says that was a MISTAKE.
He’s pointing people to a short video that explains why.
**[See what he’s warning about here.](https://links.nationalgunowner.org/a/1537/click/22610/6374453/f7f3c50e88410a5365c4482a3ddef0c184d64a45/a8e9a14b87c299c0307ef45b2a250844fc45415e) **

P.S. Some will call this alarmist — just like they did before. Decide for yourself after you see the data **[in this short video.](https://links.nationalgunowner.org/a/1537/click/22610/6374453/f7f3c50e88410a5365c4482a3ddef0c184d64a45/a8e9a14b87c299c0307ef45b2a250844fc45415e)** You don’t have to be stuck with your tinnitus forever.

Take a drive up Route 1, or Route 2, or Route 27, or really any road that doesn't lead to Portland. Try Route 7 through my old home town of Dexter. Stop at a gas station. Talk to the guy filling up his pickup. Ask him how things are going.
He'll tell you the truth. His electric bill doubled. His property tax bill went up again. His health insurance is a joke -- non-existent until he pays a deductible worth more than his truck. His kids can't afford a starter home in the town where he grew up. The mill his dad and grandad worked at has been closed for decades. His friend's logging outfit closed. The general store in his village replaced pizza and coffee with sketchy drugs and vapes, and the store -- like dozens of others in rural Maine -- is owned by a guy from out of state who doesn't speak English.
Then ask him who's looking out for him in Augusta.
He'll laugh.
That laugh -- bitter, exhausted, a little bit angry -- is the most honest political polling data in the State of Maine. It tells you everything you need to know about the relationship between the people who actually live here and the people who claim to govern in their name. Because the working Mainer, the lobsterman, the schoolteacher, the nurse, the farmer, the deputy sheriff -- all of them have figured out something that the nerd journalists at the State House or in TV newsrooms are all oblivious to.
The political class running this state -- almost all of them lifelong Democrats -- have stopped representing the people of Maine.
They represent somebody else now. Several somebody elses, in fact. They represent migrants who don't speak English and are getting EBT cards and phony drivers licenses rather than jobs. They represent New York hedge funds that own Maine solar farms. They represent a sovereign wealth fund in New Zealand that wants to make a fortune on the King Pine wind farm. They represent Big Cannabis (including the Chinese cartels). They represent Michael Bloomberg's gun-control lobby, and Planned Parenthood, and Equality Maine, and the multiplicity of crony capitalists masquerading as green energy advocates. Rather than representing the people of Maine, they're doing whatever it takes for the political class to make a buck at our expense -- or for people like Janet Mills and Shenna Bellows to accumulate more power. They represent everyone, in short, except the people who pay the taxes and live with the results.

## The Welfare State for Everyone but You
Start with MaineCare. Most people don't know the difference between Medicaid and Medicare, but it's critical to understand how MaineCare works because it's our largest and most pernicious welfare program. As I've documented at length, MaineCare is on course to bankrupt this state if something isn't done about the rampant fraud, the pathetic eligibility requirements, and the insane mismanagement coming from the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS).
In 2019, Gov. Janet Mills' first official act was to expand MaineCare -- Maine's version of Medicaid -- to roughly 100,000 new enrollees, almost all of them able-bodied childless adults. In 2022, Mills and Democratic lawmakers expanded MaineCare again, this time to a broader class of noncitizens. Maine's population stayed essentially flat from 2015 to 2025. Yet according to the Kaiser Family Foundation, MaineCare enrollment exploded from approximately 278,000 in 2015 to nearly 400,000 in 2025. The program grew by 50 percent between 2019 and 2023 alone.
The cost of all of this lands on you. Federal Medicaid dollars don't pay for noncitizen coverage in most circumstances. That tab gets picked up by Maine's General Fund -- the same general fund that pays for road salt, the State Police, and the public defenders the state can't seem to find. Every dollar Augusta sends to a non-resident's MaineCare coverage and emergency room bill is a dollar that doesn't go to the working Mainer who's been paying income taxes, sales taxes, and property taxes for forty years. Even Medicaid coverage for actual U.S. citizens imposes a significant cost on Maine, making the program our single largest expense every budget season.
Hospitals in rural Maine are closing up shop. Good luck finding a place north of Bangor to have a baby. Heaven forbid you need an ambulance somewhere around Mattawamkeag. Yet despite the obvious and undeniable deterioration of the health care that heritage Mainers rely on, Augusta's focus has been on funding handouts for illegal aliens who entered the U.S. under former President Joe Biden (D) and lodged phony asylum claims with the Dept. of Justice. The Democrat majority is more interested in shipping free needles to our cities than in providing Maine kids with quality pediatricians and clean parks to play in.
To give one poignant example from a no-bid contract that the Mills administration attempted to illegally withhold from a Freedom of Access Act request I submitted: Maine spent [$766,327](https://substack.com/redirect/a37d67a0-e29d-47b3-bb78-76733abcfa18?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) -- under a no-bid contract -- to house a single noncitizen in an Oakland memory-care facility, according to state records. The Department of Health and Human Services acknowledged on the contract itself that the individual "is and will remain ineligible" for federal Medicaid because of immigration status. Translation: Mainers paid the whole bill.
It's a story so ludicrous I wouldn't even believe it if I had found the documents myself while scanning the thousands of no-bid contracts which -- again -- the Mills administration attempted to illegally withhold from me.

## The Solar Tax
Now turn to your electric bill.
Look at the line item called "stranded costs." That money does not pay for the wires that keep your refrigerator running. It does not pay for tree-trimming. It does not pay for the linemen who climb poles in February ice storms.
That money pays for solar farms -- those black cadmium telluride-laced monstrosities shrouding once-productive farm land throughout rural Maine.
Specifically, it pays for the difference between what Central Maine Power (CMP) and Versant are forced to pay solar developers -- a premium price set by the state -- and what the resulting electricity actually fetches on the wholesale market. Maine's two big utilities are required by state law to buy that electricity at a loss. They recoup the loss through stranded-cost charges added to your bill. Maine's Office of the Public Advocate has estimated the program, known as Net Energy Billing, cost ratepayers approximately $220 million in 2025 and is projected to top $234 million in 2026. The total exposure across the program's lifetime will reach into the billions -- and that doesn't include the cost our children and grandchildren will eat when its time to recycle all that toxic waste.
Eighty-six percent of Maine residential ratepayers receive no benefit from the program at all. They just pay the bill. The Office of the Public Advocate has estimated that as little as 15 percent of NEB costs ever return to subscribers in the form of lower bills. The rest is profit for the developers.
Who are those developers? According to a 2023 Maine Wire analysis of Maine Public Utilities Commission records, 88 percent of the firms profiting from net energy billing are headquartered out of state. The Solar Tax and NEB is the equivalent of a massive wormhole sucking money out of Mainers bank accounts and depositing into the hands of wealthy developers in New York, Minnesota, California, and Massachusetts.
Then there's the Renewable Energy Credits, or RECs, the green energy boondoggle that undergirds all the other green energy boondoggles. If you're unfamiliar with RECs, they're like the IOUs that Lloyd and Harry use in _Dumb and Dumber,_ except they form the basis of New England's entire power-grid. Every kilowatt-hour generated at a Maine solar facility produces a "credit" -- again, an imaginary monopoly money figment of our collective imaginations -- that the developer can sell to a power company in another state -- say, a coal plant in Massachusetts looking to greenwash its books. When that REC is sold out of state, Maine's contribution to the climate, on paper, gets credited to that other state.
The result is that everyone pretends that the solar field in Augusta is magically lowering the carbon footprint of an office park in Worcester. Of course, it's all a bunch of make-believe horseshit. It makes the liberals feel good, and some of them genuinely believe this nonsense is helping to change the weather. But the cost of making naive liberals feel good is higher electricity costs for every single rate-payer in Maine -- costs that are hoovered out of the state for the benefit of anyone but Mainers.
This is a regressive tax. The lowest-income Mainer in Madawaska -- who can't afford a $30,000 rooftop solar system or a buy-in to a community solar farm -- is subsidizing the affluent suburbanite in Cape Elizabeth who can. The U.S. Energy Information Administration ranks Maine's residential electricity prices among the six highest in the country. The socialists in Portland, for all their prattling about helping the poor, have never seriously interrogated the morality of jacking up electric costs on working class Mainers so wealthy out of state developers can make a buck.
Now the wind. The much-heralded King Pine Wind project in Aroostook County would, if completed, become the largest onshore wind farm east of the Mississippi River. Its developer, Boston-based Longroad Energy, is -- according to its own corporate filings reviewed by The Maine Wire -- 92 percent owned by foreign investors. Forty percent belongs to the New Zealand Superannuation Fund, the sovereign wealth fund of New Zealand's national pension system. Another 40 percent is owned by Infratil Limited, a Wellington-based infrastructure firm (also based in New Zealand, for those who are unfamiliar). The remaining 12 percent of foreign ownership belongs to MEAG, a German asset management company. Maine ratepayers and Massachusetts ratepayers will fund the project. The profits will flow to retirees in Wellington and asset managers in Munich.
The same political class that lectures Mainers about "energy independence" handed the keys to the Aroostook County energy grid to a foreign sovereign wealth fund. It's a Troy Jackson special, but plenty of Aroostook County Republicans left their finger-prints on that one, too, falling for the bogus claim that helping enrich the Kiwis might create a spare job or two in The County.

## The Office of New Americans
In August 2023, Gov. Mills issued an executive order directing her Office of Policy, Innovation and the Future -- run by Hannah Pingree, daughter of U.S. Rep. Chellie Pingree (D-Maine) and current candidate for governor -- to plan a state office to handle migrant resettlement and integration. The companion bill, LD 2167, sponsored by Rep. Deqa Dhalac (D-South Portland), failed to pass on the merits. So Democratic lawmakers stuffed it into the supplemental budget on the final day of the session and passed the funding on a party-line vote.
The stated purpose of the Office of New Americans is to help Maine attract 75,000 new workers -- many of them immigrants -- by 2030. In every other state where an Office of New Americans has been created, the promises begin the same: Jobs! Economic growth! Diversity is our strength! But the invariable conclusion is a new express super highway to the welfare office -- but with signs in Arabic, Portuguese, Somali, French, and Lingala. And then the EBT cards and free health care blossoms into free college, special tax incentives, low interest loans, and every other benefit under the sun. But only for "New Americans" -- paid for by Old Americans, aka you and me.
There are problems with this plan that the Mills administration would prefer you not think about.
The first is that the math on workforce participation doesn't work. Maine's workforce participation rate is among the lowest in the country. Tens of thousands of working-age Mainers are already out of the labor force. The premise that Maine "needs" foreign labor presupposes that nothing can be done to bring those people back into the economy -- that, for instance, you can't reform welfare programs that pay more than entry-level work, or address the cost-of-living crisis that drives families across the New Hampshire line, or stop punishing employers with one of the highest per-capita tax burdens in the country.
The second problem is the governor's own admission. In a 2022 debate, Mills told voters Maine "needed" asylum seekers in part because, in her words, businesses needed workers. But under federal law, asylum seekers may not legally work for at least 180 days after filing their petition. Many petitions are denied, and the asylum-grant rate hovers around 14 percent. So the people Mills said Maine "needed" to fill jobs were, by federal law, prohibited from doing the very thing she said the state needed them to do. And those who do get work approvals are refusing to get jobs. That's not my opinion. That's what Mills asserted in a recent budget bill introduced last year. By her count, some 4,000 to 5,000 "New Mainers" are enjoying EBT cards and refusing to get jobs even though they have work permits.
In the meantime, Maine taxpayers fund their housing, their MaineCare, their General Assistance, and a state-issued procurement contract for English-language instruction at $159 per student seat -- a no-bid contract for adult "multilingual learners," according to Department of Education procurement justification forms reviewed by The Maine Wire. More than half of all adult education students in Maine, by the department's own admission, are learning English. In some southern Maine public schools, the rates are even higher.
The first director of the Office of New Americans, Tarlan Ahmadov, resigned in April 2025 after Maine Wire reporting raised questions about his anti-Armenian social media activity, his apparent role on a state-lawmaker junket to Azerbaijan funded in part by the Azeri government, and the possibility that he had functioned as an unregistered foreign agent. Mills had appointed him in December 2024. The office she rammed into existence to help "New Mainers" was, almost from the start, beset by precisely the kind of scandal you'd expect from an institution built around political ideology rather than the actual interests of the people of Maine.

## Politics as Career Ladder
It would be one thing if all of this were the result of sincere ideological conviction -- misguided, perhaps, but at least honest. The truth is more sordid. Increasingly, Maine's elected leadership treats the apparatus of state government as a career runway. State gigs, elected or appointed, have become opportunities the feather nests and reward friends. The old idea of a public _servant_ is a sick joke.
Gov. Mills, term-limited, announced her bid for the Democratic nomination to challenge Sen. Susan Collins in October 2025. Her policy agenda for the past three years has been, in significant measure, the agenda of a candidate audition tape: the trans-rights showdown with the Trump White House, the social-media set pieces, the studious refusal to engage with the substance of any of the scandals piling up in her own administration. She's running toward Washington, D.C., and away from a fiscal house that's absolutely ablaze, and rural communities beset with drug addiction and organized crime.
Maine Secretary of State Shenna Bellows (D), the official charged with administering the elections, declared her own candidacy for governor and as of this writing has refused to step aside. She is now positioned to oversee her own primary, in an office that has previously written ballot questions in language that referendum campaigns described as misleading. She has hired Marc Elias -- Hillary Clinton's former lawyer -- and her campaign has paid his firm at least $12,000, according to campaign finance filings. In February 2026, she admitted on camera that noncitizens are registered to vote in Maine, then refused to cooperate with a U.S. Department of Justice request for the state's voter rolls. Then she very intentionally partnered with the Community Organizing Alliance, a dark money group connected to both Gateway Community Services and the Maine People's Alliance, and a group whose sole purpose is to recruit migrant voters.
Bellows couldn't make it any clearer that her path to great power lies not in winning over the hearts and minds of voters, but in making payola promises to the very "New Mainers" she's illegally entered into ballot harvesting operations.
Speaker of the House Ryan Fecteau (D-Biddeford), meanwhile, sponsored LD 1082 in 2025 -- a bill to raise real-estate transfer taxes on property sales over $1 million, with proceeds funneled to subsidized housing programs. Fecteau is employed by Avesta Housing, one of the largest affordable-housing developers in northern New England and a likely beneficiary of his bill. The bill was rolled into the supplemental budget rather than debated on the floor. Did other lawmakers get the courtesy of bestowing massive financial windfalls on their businesses or their companies?
Senate President Mattie Daughtry (D-Cumberland) co-sponsored that bill. She's no stranger to using her position in state government to funnel taxpayer dollars into her own business interests. Around the same time Janet Mills was harassing and threatening Rick Savage of Sunday River Brewing Company, Daughtry was securing a $500,000 payout from the Finance Authority of Maine, one of the largest payments given under the Thrive II program. Savage ended up selling his business and fleeing Mills Covid-19 tyranny, but Daughtry mediocre beer company continues to reap the rewards of political favoritism.
This is not democracy. This is the politics of personal enrichment.
## So What Now
Now we come to the part where, in a normal column, the writer offers a hopeful conclusion.
I am not going to do that. The situation is what it is. Mainers are paying more for everything -- power, housing, health insurance, food, gas -- while their state government writes checks to people who don't live here, didn't grow up here, and in many cases don't speak English. The only thing that's gotten cheaper in eight years is the cannabis, and that's only because it's triad weed laced with organophosphate poisons. The state's largest welfare program is being defrauded. The state's energy policy is making a foreign pension fund rich. The state's immigration policy is being run by an office that didn't get a real legislative vote, for the benefit of politicians who want to change demographics to architect a permanent majority. The state's election rules are being administered by a candidate who openly brags about illegally rigging presidential elections. The state's house speaker is writing tax bills that benefit his employer.
The remedy is not complicated. Maine choose our current path. Returning to the way life should be will require making new decisions and new choices.
First, Maine must have regime change. Not just one or two offices, but a cleansing wave driven by voters who are sick a tired of corruption. That's the hard part. Then the agenda gets simpler: End net energy billing. Investigate MaineCare fraud and prosecute it. Stop funding services that bypass the federal immigration system. Make Maine a place where you can build a house without ten layers of permits. Hold elected officials to the same conflict-of-interest rules they enforce on everyone else. Cut taxes on the people who actually pay them. Let working Mainers keep more of what they earn.
You don't need a 600-page strategic plan from a D.C. consulting firm to figure that out. You need lawmakers who are loyal to the State of Maine and the people who live here -- the Old Mainers.
That used to be a low bar. In Augusta in 2026, it has become revolutionary.
The guy at the gas station up on Route 27 already understands all of this. He's understood it for years. The question is whether enough of the rest of us will figure it out before there's nothing left of Maine to save.
The state is yours. Take it back.

His kids can't afford a starter home in the town where he grew up. The mill his dad and grandad worked at has been closed for decades. His friend's logging outfit closed. The general store in his village replaced pizza and coffee with sketchy drugs and vapes, and the store -- like dozens of others in rural Maine -- is owned by a guy from out of state who doesn't speak English. Then ask him who's looking out for him in Augusta. He'll laugh. That laugh -- bitter, exhausted, a little bit angry -- is the most honest political polling data in the State of Maine. It tells you everything you need to know about the relationship between the people who actually live here and the people who claim to govern in their name. Because the working Mainer, the lobsterman, the schoolteacher, the nurse, the farmer, the deputy sheriff -- all of them have figured out something that the nerd journalists at the State House or in TV newsrooms are all oblivious to. The political class running this state -- almost all of them lifelong Democrats -- have stopped representing the people of Maine. They represent somebody else now. Several somebody elses, in fact. They represent migrants who don't speak English and are getting EBT cards and phony drivers licenses rather than jobs. They represent New York hedge funds that own Maine solar farms. They represent a sovereign wealth fund in New Zealand that wants to make a fortune on the King Pine wind farm. They represent Big Cannabis (including the Chinese cartels). They represent Michael Bloomberg's gun-control lobby, and Planned Parenthood, and Equality Maine, and the multiplicity of crony capitalists masquerading as green energy advocates. Rather than representing the people of Maine, they're doing whatever it takes for the political class to make a buck at our expense -- or for people like Janet Mills and Shenna Bellows to accumulate more power. They represent everyone, in short, except the people who pay the taxes and live with the results. Sign up to get The Robinson Report delivered FREE to your inbox!!! The Welfare State for Everyone but You Start with MaineCare. Most people don't know the difference between Medicaid and Medicare, but it's critical to understand how MaineCare works because it's our largest and most pernicious welfare program. As I've documented at length, MaineCare is on course to bankrupt this state if something isn't done about the rampant fraud, the pathetic eligibility requirements, and the insane mismanagement coming from the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS). In 2019, Gov. Janet Mills' first official act was to expand MaineCare -- Maine's version of Medicaid -- to roughly 100,000 new enrollees, almost all of them able-bodied childless adults. In 2022, Mills and Democratic lawmakers expanded MaineCare again, this time to a broader class of noncitizens. Maine's population stayed essentially flat from 2015 to 2025. Yet according to the Kaiser Family Foundation, MaineCare enrollment exploded from approximately 278,000 in 2015 to nearly 400,000 in 2025. The program grew by 50 percent between 2019 and 2023 alone. The cost of all of this lands on you. Federal Medicaid dollars don't pay for noncitizen coverage in most circumstances. That tab gets picked up by Maine's General Fund -- the same general fund that pays for road salt, the State Police, and the public defenders the state can't seem to find. Every dollar Augusta sends to a non-resident's MaineCare coverage and emergency room bill is a dollar that doesn't go to the working Mainer who's been paying income taxes, sales taxes, and property taxes for forty years. Even Medicaid coverage for actual U.S. citizens imposes a significant cost on Maine, making the program our single largest expense every budget season. Hospitals in rural Maine are closing up shop. Good luck finding a place north of Bangor to have a baby. Heaven forbid you need an ambulance somewhere around Mattawamkeag. Yet despite the obvious and undeniable deterioration of the health care that heritage Mainers rely on, Augusta's focus has been on funding handouts for illegal aliens who entered the U.S. under former President Joe Biden (D) and lodged phony asylum claims with the Dept. of Justice. The Democrat majority is more interested in shipping free needles to our cities than in providing Maine kids with quality pediatricians and clean parks to play in. To give one poignant example from a no-bid contract that the Mills administration attempted to illegally withhold from a Freedom of Access Act request I submitted: Maine spent -- under a no-bid contract -- to house a single noncitizen in an Oakland memory-care facility, according to state records. The Department of Health and Human Services acknowledged on the contract itself that the individual "is and will remain ineligible" for federal Medicaid because of immigration status. Translation: Mainers paid the whole bill. It's a story so ludicrous I wouldn't even believe it if I had found the documents myself while scanning the thousands of no-bid contracts which -- again -- the Mills administration attempted to illegally withhold from me. 27k New Englanders subscribe to The Robinson Report. You should too... The Solar Tax Now turn to your electric bill. Look at the line item called "stranded costs." That money does not pay for the wires that keep your refrigerator running. It does not pay for tree-trimming. It does not pay for the linemen who climb poles in February ice storms. That money pays for solar farms -- those black cadmium telluride-laced monstrosities shrouding once-productive farm land throughout rural Maine. Specifically, it pays for the difference between what Central Maine Power (CMP) and Versant are forced to pay solar developers -- a premium price set by the state -- and what the resulting electricity actually fetches on the wholesale market. Maine's two big utilities are required by state law to buy that electricity at a loss. They recoup the loss through stranded-cost charges added to your bill. Maine's Office of the Public Advocate has estimated the program, known as Net Energy Billing, cost ratepayers approximately $220 million in 2025 and is projected to top $234 million in 2026. The total exposure across the program's lifetime will reach into the billions -- and that doesn't include the cost our children and grandchildren will eat when its time to recycle all that toxic waste. Eighty-six percent of Maine residential ratepayers receive no benefit from the program at all. They just pay the bill. The Office of the Public Advocate has estimated that as little as 15 percent of NEB costs ever return to subscribers in the form of lower bills. The rest is profit for the developers. Who are those developers? According to a 2023 Maine Wire analysis of Maine Public Utilities Commission records, 88 percent of the firms profiting from net energy billing are headquartered out of state. The Solar Tax and NEB is the equivalent of a massive wormhole sucking money out of Mainers bank accounts and depositing into the hands of wealthy developers in New York, Minnesota, California, and Massachusetts. Then there's the Renewable Energy Credits, or RECs, the green energy boondoggle that undergirds all the other green energy boondoggles. If you're unfamiliar with RECs, they're like the IOUs that Lloyd and Harry use in Dumb and Dumber, except they form the basis of New England's entire power-grid. Every kilowatt-hour generated at a Maine solar facility produces a "credit" -- again, an imaginary monopoly money figment of our collective imaginations -- that the developer can sell to a power company in another state -- say, a coal plant in Massachusetts looking to greenwash its books. When that REC is sold out of state, Maine's contribution to the climate, on paper, gets credited to that other state. The result is that everyone pretends that the solar field in Augusta is magically lowering the carbon footprint of an office park in Worcester. Of course, it's all a bunch of make-believe horseshit. It makes the liberals feel good, and some of them genuinely believe this nonsense is helping to change the weather. But the cost of making naive liberals feel good is higher electricity costs for every single rate-payer in Maine -- costs that are hoovered out of the state for the benefit of anyone but Mainers. This is a regressive tax. The lowest-income Mainer in Madawaska -- who can't afford a $30,000 rooftop solar system or a buy-in to a community solar farm -- is subsidizing the affluent suburbanite in Cape Elizabeth who can. The U.S. Energy Information Administration ranks Maine's residential electricity prices among the six highest in the country. The socialists in Portland, for all their prattling about helping the poor, have never seriously interrogated the morality of jacking up electric costs on working class Mainers so wealthy out of state developers can make a buck. Now the wind. The much-heralded King Pine Wind project in Aroostook County would, if completed, become the largest onshore wind farm east of the Mississippi River. Its developer, Boston-based Longroad Energy, is -- according to its own corporate filings reviewed by The Maine Wire -- 92 percent owned by foreign investors. Forty percent belongs to the New Zealand Superannuation Fund, the sovereign wealth fund of New Zealand's national pension system. Another 40 percent is owned by Infratil Limited, a Wellington-based infrastructure firm (also based in New Zealand, for those who are unfamiliar). The remaining 12 percent of foreign ownership belongs to MEAG, a German asset management company. Maine ratepayers and Massachusetts ratepayers will fund the project. The profits will flow to retirees in Wellington and asset managers in Munich. The same political class that lectures Mainers about "energy independence" handed the keys to the Aroostook County energy grid to a foreign sovereign wealth fund. It's a Troy Jackson special, but plenty of Aroostook County Republicans left their finger-prints on that one, too, falling for the bogus claim that helping enrich the Kiwis might create a spare job or two in The County. Thanks for reading! This post is public so feel free to share it. The Office of New Americans In August 2023, Gov. Mills issued an executive order directing her Office of Policy, Innovation and the Future -- run by Hannah Pingree, daughter of U.S. Rep. Chellie Pingree (D-Maine) and current candidate for governor -- to plan a state office to handle migrant resettlement and integration. The companion bill, LD 2167, sponsored by Rep. Deqa Dhalac (D-South Portland), failed to pass on the merits. So Democratic lawmakers stuffed it into the supplemental budget on the final day of the session and passed the funding on a party-line vote. The stated purpose of the Office of New Americans is to help Maine attract 75,000 new workers -- many of them immigrants -- by 2030. In every other state where an Office of New Americans has been created, the promises begin the same: Jobs! Economic growth! Diversity is our strength! But the invariable conclusion is a new express super highway to the welfare office -- but with signs in Arabic, Portuguese, Somali, French, and Lingala. And then the EBT cards and free health care blossoms into free college, special tax incentives, low interest loans, and every other benefit under the sun. But only for "New Americans" -- paid for by Old Americans, aka you and me. There are problems with this plan that the Mills administration would prefer you not think about. The first is that the math on workforce participation doesn't work. Maine's workforce participation rate is among the lowest in the country. Tens of thousands of working-age Mainers are already out of the labor force. The premise that Maine "needs" foreign labor presupposes that nothing can be done to bring those people back into the economy -- that, for instance, you can't reform welfare programs that pay more than entry-level work, or address the cost-of-living crisis that drives families across the New Hampshire line, or stop punishing employers with one of the highest per-capita tax burdens in the country. The second problem is the governor's own admission. In a 2022 debate, Mills told voters Maine "needed" asylum seekers in part because, in her words, businesses needed workers. But under federal law, asylum seekers may not legally work for at least 180 days after filing their petition. Many petitions are denied, and the asylum-grant rate hovers around 14 percent. So the people Mills said Maine "needed" to fill jobs were, by federal law, prohibited from doing the very thing she said the state needed them to do. And those who do get work approvals are refusing to get jobs. That's not my opinion. That's what Mills asserted in a recent budget bill introduced last year. By her count, some 4,000 to 5,000 "New Mainers" are enjoying EBT cards and refusing to get jobs even though they have work permits. In the meantime, Maine taxpayers fund their housing, their MaineCare, their General Assistance, and a state-issued procurement contract for English-language instruction at $159 per student seat -- a no-bid contract for adult "multilingual learners," according to Department of Education procurement justification forms reviewed by The Maine Wire. More than half of all adult education students in Maine, by the department's own admission, are learning English. In some southern Maine public schools, the rates are even higher. The first director of the Office of New Americans, Tarlan Ahmadov, resigned in April 2025 after Maine Wire reporting raised questions about his anti-Armenian social media activity, his apparent role on a state-lawmaker junket to Azerbaijan funded in part by the Azeri government, and the possibility that he had functioned as an unregistered foreign agent. Mills had appointed him in December 2024. The office she rammed into existence to help "New Mainers" was, almost from the start, beset by precisely the kind of scandal you'd expect from an institution built around political ideology rather than the actual interests of the people of Maine. The Medicaid Fraud Reckoning This brings us to MaineCare. What was supposed to be an anti-poverty welfare program to help the poor afford health care has become a cash machine spitting millions into the pockets of "New Mainer" fraudsters. Where are all the Mainers who've been helped by the billions in new Medicaid spending and the massive tax increases to cover the inevitable cost overruns? We've covered, and will continue to cover, the lewd and lascivious theft of Maine tax dollars by foreign fraudsters, but you can read my summation piece here: | | | | * ---|---|--- | Apr 27 | Politics as Career Ladder It would be one thing if all of this were the result of sincere ideological conviction -- misguided, perhaps, but at least honest. The truth is more sordid. Increasingly, Maine's elected leadership treats the apparatus of state government as a career runway. State gigs, elected or appointed, have become opportunities the feather nests and reward friends. The old idea of a public servant is a sick joke. Gov. Mills, term-limited, announced her bid for the Democratic nomination to challenge Sen. Susan Collins in October 2025. Her policy agenda for the past three years has been, in significant measure, the agenda of a candidate audition tape: the trans-rights showdown with the Trump White House, the social-media set pieces, the studious refusal to engage with the substance of any of the scandals piling up in her own administration. She's running toward Washington, D.C., and away from a fiscal house that's absolutely ablaze, and rural communities beset with drug addiction and organized crime. Maine Secretary of State Shenna Bellows (D), the official charged with administering the elections, declared her own candidacy for governor and as of this writing has refused to step aside. She is now positioned to oversee her own primary, in an office that has previously written ballot questions in language that referendum campaigns described as misleading. She has hired Marc Elias -- Hillary Clinton's former lawyer -- and her campaign has paid his firm at least $12,000, according to campaign finance filings. In February 2026, she admitted on camera that noncitizens are registered to vote in Maine, then refused to cooperate with a U.S. Department of Justice request for the state's voter rolls. Then she very intentionally partnered with the Community Organizing Alliance, a dark money group connected to both Gateway Community Services and the Maine People's Alliance, and a group whose sole purpose is to recruit migrant voters. Bellows couldn't make it any clearer that her path to great power lies not in winning over the hearts and minds of voters, but in making payola promises to the very "New Mainers" she's illegally entered into ballot harvesting operations. Speaker of the House Ryan Fecteau (D-Biddeford), meanwhile, sponsored LD 1082 in 2025 -- a bill to raise real-estate transfer taxes on property sales over $1 million, with proceeds funneled to subsidized housing programs. Fecteau is employed by Avesta Housing, one of the largest affordable-housing developers in northern New England and a likely beneficiary of his bill. The bill was rolled into the supplemental budget rather than debated on the floor. Did other lawmakers get the courtesy of bestowing massive financial windfalls on their businesses or their companies? Senate President Mattie Daughtry (D-Cumberland) co-sponsored that bill. She's no stranger to using her position in state government to funnel taxpayer dollars into her own business interests. Around the same time Janet Mills was harassing and threatening Rick Savage of Sunday River Brewing Company, Daughtry was securing a $500,000 payout from the Finance Authority of Maine, one of the largest payments given under the Thrive II program. Savage ended up selling his business and fleeing Mills Covid-19 tyranny, but Daughtry mediocre beer company continues to reap the rewards of political favoritism. This is not democracy. This is the politics of personal enrichment. So What Now Now we come to the part where, in a normal column, the writer offers a hopeful conclusion. I am not going to do that. The situation is what it is. Mainers are paying more for everything -- power, housing, health insurance, food, gas -- while their state government writes checks to people who don't live here, didn't grow up here, and in many cases don't speak English. The only thing that's gotten cheaper in eight years is the cannabis, and that's only because it's triad weed laced with organophosphate poisons. The state's largest welfare program is being defrauded. The state's energy policy is making a foreign pension fund rich. The state's immigration policy is being run by an office that didn't get a real legislative vote, for the benefit of politicians who want to change demographics to architect a permanent majority. The state's election rules are being administered by a candidate who openly brags about illegally rigging presidential elections. The state's house speaker is writing tax bills that benefit his employer. The remedy is not complicated. Maine choose our current path. Returning to the way life should be will require making new decisions and new choices. First, Maine must have regime change. Not just one or two offices, but a cleansing wave driven by voters who are sick a tired of corruption. That's the hard part. Then the agenda gets simpler: End net energy billing. Investigate MaineCare fraud and prosecute it. Stop funding services that bypass the federal immigration system. Make Maine a place where you can build a house without ten layers of permits. Hold elected officials to the same conflict-of-interest rules they enforce on everyone else. Cut taxes on the people who actually pay them. Let working Mainers keep more of what they earn. You don't need a 600-page strategic plan from a D.C. consulting firm to figure that out. You need lawmakers who are loyal to the State of Maine and the people who live here -- the Old Mainers. That used to be a low bar. In Augusta in 2026, it has become revolutionary. The guy at the gas station up on Route 27 already understands all of this. He's understood it for years. The question is whether enough of the rest of us will figure it out before there's nothing left of Maine to save. The state is yours. Take it back. ? You 're receiving The Robinson Report for free. ## Comey Indicted Over Seashell Post
Former FBI Director James Comey was [indicted again Tuesday,](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0DGOszAQBeDTmM7IGQZsChd_Q5e_3RIZe0gmMjjC3iBuvwJpT7DdSCO9p-993ce748jr479byJY5jSvtOVIptI0-LXTwGtgXCu7heJ29_-TAIyjopEIJ_Rgcx2PEKtiZCKipyN601thqQKyeNqDp0PSalPH9hE1LFIhuyhskMJ2p2J5pCqG_KaWhqR263pFp5radaPJGoKLAJW31K_FanjTHI31oq31aqmifpbyzaP4JGAQM-77Xfsqn4vwLGM5TwPByC2V5keSvSV4oOR3y9Z0Le5KB3kXAUG02vHeOkXOnBarH4jhefeVPI30s_AQAAP__RUd8sA) this time over a 2025 Instagram photo of seashells spelling "86 47," which President Trump's allies said was meant as a threat against the president. The indictment, [filed in North Carolina](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGu4yAQBdCvsTsiPAY7KSi2Sfe23dIawxDPEwYL5sXK368Sab9g2xnp6p7752v5Qk6cH79xJyexLJnOlkiE6uLLTi_Ogb1QwAdyjt4_W-AFNExKGwW3JSCn12L64CIR0NiTG-Z5NnYGY_rNrXaIVw8TWa3XMA1WhzXeJnsd59UO1vfs3mnawG3QeobxggZvSNcxWrvS6q-d0RRYSr18F86yUUyv8qR68WXvk9tEjtaNvzq4d3A_z_OSV_9WvP8d3I-SWNi3Du7fP03Ykwp0YJWdsryPuFNTH6v6h1WNsG2Ukjq2IkWVGNkzpqYaclCyVUKhTEFJ_dkPVX1GMLMG6KsLx8kpcZvmzujHjpw-TeW_5n06-BsAAP__opySkw), where Comey owns a beach house, marks the Justice Department's second federal case against him in seven months. Comey [deleted the post](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFuwyAYBOCnsTcs_APGHhi6eEvXjhaGn-SPMFiGxs3bV4nUJ-h80p2--7osF0uR0vXTbmhqyEvCs0SsFY_F5Q2flDy5it5eLaXg3KN4WoDDwLhkMC3eUnwusvUmIAKKFk2vtZZKg5TtzQQ9jGoawYq-D1IoOVklYVQovfDrNLRkXm1cwtRzrkF0VtrJ4iiCUiuubmwkR081H909U6o3DPGZH3h0Lm9tNLda99KIjwbmBubzPLuQf16KV97AvOdIlVxpYL7bDQt7s9ifi71hLOHJ7t-lkkPmcbdH3TBVth95xfYwfj8pRiqDbiS_bpbie73-67KHgd8AAAD__zUsgnU) within hours, saying he didn't realize "86" could mean violence. Trump is the 47th president; "86" is slang for getting rid of someone. A federal judge dismissed Comey's first indictment in November after ruling the prosecutor was unlawfully appointed.
## UAE Announces Surprise Exit from OPEC
The United Arab Emirates announced Tuesday [it will depart OPEC](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0D1uhDAQxfHTmA5khsGGwkUauk2bEvljWCYy9gqcRdw-IldI96Qn_Yr_12N-WI6cnp92I1OWPCc6j0il0D77vNHFKbAvFOzTclq8fx-BZ5Cgaok1jHOwHK8Zq2AWIqCuItNqrbHXgFitBmFUvRo8OU3oOgUtkVSt7MfRqU5jxebWJMLYSqmhayza0dLQLX3vyPlBoKTAJe_Nd-ZUVlrild-0Nz5vVTRrKa9DdB8CJgHTeZ6NT87fp4DppgVMEu89CJh-LNX5Rb7OHGvebWrWssVqN-F1cox8KC1QPjfL8c8v_4ryNvAbAAD__5ufc2U) effective May 1, dealing a major blow to the long-standing oil cartel. The UAE was the third-largest producer in OPEC behind Saudi Arabia and Iraq. The loss could create disarray within the group, which has always tried to show a united front despite disagreements over production quotas. The surprise announcement comes after the UAE was the target of missile and drone attacks for weeks by fellow OPEC member Iran. ---
Hey ya'll,
In Washington, DC, and especially here in Louisiana, I've been seeing a lot of the same old, same old.
If you are paying attention, I know you are seeing it too.
We're seeing the same cruelty, corruption, and injustices that people have been confronting and working against for a long time.
So, this year, I think we need something different here in Louisiana and in Washington--a candidate with a different life experience than the average politician.
I have spent my life working in fields, growing food, and running a family business, growing up as the grandson of a sharecropper in rural Louisiana.
We don't often see that kind of life experience represented in Washington.
It seems these days in politics, we don't see many everyday people in the places where big decisions are being made.
And that's why a lot of the same bad decisions are getting made.
And I know what some of y'all might be thinking:
How's the Farmer gonna win a Senate race? In Louisiana?
Let me tell you a couple of reasons why a farmer can win.
Because a farmer knows what it's like to struggle. This farmer would never betray the millions of Americans struggling to make it in a system that wasn't designed for everyone.
Because a farmer knows that true prosperity only comes from peace. And this farmer would never send another person's child to die in a senseless war.
Because a farmer like me, grandson of a sharecropper, knows that a good education, pre-K through college or trade, is a right everyone should have.
Because farmers know how important it is that all of our children grow up in schools that support their vision and help them be the best versions of themselves, whether they want to farm fields or go to Washington.
I'm working to do both.
