I’m starting to gain some traction in the race for Minnesota Senate, and so my political opponents are starting to go negative on me. | [](http://links.ourdefenseofamerica.com/u/click?_t=aa3ef0db03454a26b650c9ca7e919386&_m=34349a1624b941fb80c731eeb12d9e89&_e=E3aSuB5XB-ZYsyh_y9PhHPGPtud5LmPcE46rDIoWwqBl7YiEpHefwKjhwOm6IOnmJ-abHCkX0Niw8SIcpOEUb4fpC0MXxWgSORHhcfGzpbVBxnoNdm5bYTfggFOAUT2JI9m845728O9zRRoFFaQl7kbLDX1ApX-x1NwjaFkF4XpTTU4iS24R52YztWMdHgrLOHC-BT833mp552tDYpbV3KbRl_xajalDcZNRYEHivOqaf921-na0F_Woix-uSr3fd1OmChnKuLF5kVFL6LYKfDXMepPDZOq70RmuBXqUAorkvfIJ2OO_e4wVdDQVTI-kQVJ6h_Yecsx4ibjfKorjnvDkzoF6T3hiLMGWkAQ8Nw4T48YmMac5GpcX-y2kaJAQGYzMGJV2KKkQT_bmMhJxEm806KSUDaHPxmX47A1zb38oSF_ucBG5sM1LOMaFUShuTynzvC8_e9m0q4VBcFo5t4GE544C5BlHOJ1N2EhOj9i4TIveqP3gLGLKAwgMyRCazgk6gJafvHdLvGbNvaXhgqkNnlEgQCUbCSF1F1YjpR4HWAHWQC4zPYyiaMaBformkqflKB6gpmwmnICAeVkTLyNygNuHflw3-aulpNUmiFlwCNVud-QJxyp-ekKfEhMfcJF6koTfFh4v2sXHD0mysnse35qaSA9qvFry75pVb_1YU0Eqc3sJI_Jx6Afyvec5I6EraHMys5qq2WzT2iUNEUdAjDJ8g76ZENBHVKr7khTeut2L3XkcN_U1n0Mgu4tn)

---
Fellow Conservative,

**As a former Navy SEAL** , I’m used to being under attack. But the lies being told by my opponents who want to serve you in the US Senate is a new one for me. Something so sipmle that I’ve said on the campaign trail, or a position I’ve taken that my opponents may disagree with? **

It’s funny how an opponent can turn pretty much anything that comes out of a campaign into a flat out lie.
**
Though I’ve been in the Minnesota Senate race for about a year now, I’m no household name by any means. But our campaign is beginning to attract the attention of voters around the state as I continue to win straw poll after straw poll **(12 and counting now).** Over the weekend we just won the Congressional District 3 straw poll by a wide margin!

**I knew I would be attacked at some point - but I naively believed it wouldn’t be so dirty or so intense.**

_[](http://links.ourdefenseofamerica.com/u/click?_t=aa3ef0db03454a26b650c9ca7e919386&_m=34349a1624b941fb80c731eeb12d9e89&_e=E3aSuB5XB-ZYsyh_y9PhHPGPtud5LmPcE46rDIoWwqBl7YiEpHefwKjhwOm6IOnmJ-abHCkX0Niw8SIcpOEUb4fpC0MXxWgSORHhcfGzpbVBxnoNdm5bYTfggFOAUT2JI9m845728O9zRRoFFaQl7kbLDX1ApX-x1NwjaFkF4XpTTU4iS24R52YztWMdHgrLOHC-BT833mp552tDYpbV3KbRl_xajalDcZNRYEHivOqaf921-na0F_Woix-uSr3fd1OmChnKuLF5kVFL6LYKfDBV2cCbKs3gXMulKNd08rFwIow2kpMmfS5E49x5tvBROjlQS0382Uj84ZAm6_JEfNHCNoHSOEA7UrNB7jsXOBYPyMoNN0_85FHCjr0BdNq03YpZh8eREChXM0GF7y4ptT-fmjzqaYiRYd53693V3fJL7Q_1uKUTdqWL1oWupQC900AFhw6UWPkXKPE3rutiOy0BX3IkUVHYwQnXdeFbE5Bad_3qdilbHNYRBTRbnkmNK0Ia0FO0yaITKsdM-EcdMGuBHzaBeXYpuhnqQvTtLTvfSsLUDSA2cUKfeJ2QhoYULMsAXVeUNaO2Md7tnNvUi-4gxWTplgTUBXy32DzU2yJHCVi01PvwErRZ01FS_f5hogumXvlQPPPFxb2xwYK8U4kJa4fw9c3dgBv41OkyUjWySwMeBJXWQmdHXAkXCGLi2NtrbfbuTX7dqPUIcD6mtzaKyCOR_4LsIAa4vRKFFTC8uLOtvWRyb_HapzKVAFDm)_
Personally, I can take the hits. I get it, my opponents see me as a threat. But here’s the deal: the Senate seat in Minnesota is too important to let petty grievances get in the way of defeating Democrats and taking back this Senate seat for the Republican Party.

I know it may not be much to you, but **[if you’re able to chip in $5 to my people-powered campaign right now](http://links.ourdefenseofamerica.com/u/click?_t=aa3ef0db03454a26b650c9ca7e919386&_m=34349a1624b941fb80c731eeb12d9e89&_e=E3aSuB5XB-ZYsyh_y9PhHPGPtud5LmPcE46rDIoWwqBl7YiEpHefwKjhwOm6IOnmJ-abHCkX0Niw8SIcpOEUb4fpC0MXxWgSORHhcfGzpbVBxnoNdm5bYTfggFOAUT2JI9m845728O9zRRoFFaQl7kbLDX1ApX-x1NwjaFkF4XpTTU4iS24R52YztWMdHgrLOHC-BT833mp552tDYpbV3KbRl_xajalDcZNRYEHivOqaf921-na0F_Woix-uSr3fd1OmChnKuLF5kVFL6LYKfAckIblIC0BFL4rmE0rY24lJ4ogPvV1ZxW3UFOpeIiMKI-PTowtCxb1Oq43v3Hch6E8chTofT9IT5BN0KEyHwtkMZc8sYcW0iRNBCTArfOWkoIJmNy3fmpffuyK_nwzQzshQ5xW5uxhdk8rRpF0eX2_NycXg1-_MTNfBKUATh5tfujoPTcx8jXEZUg0bjGhiOPnulgbWF4DgQ7jdmOJ2fBLGLSWfsOBkJIrGN7FBrecNW0MEeCFc_TKaB00hFQorKfnjIsT0XfAHqWQM4_wUysXFj7wPjnhhhWn1uS4t0r1_b5CEMzxq92pkuvKwkx4PN_czIwaTTbDQ2N6zg2UC4_N65wizKzz5r9sG9amSTTwEXy4V9K_hCzbyG8RI2dN56ppMlRemOcDgpdtaCYjHS05IiC7oIe8muVEUdxWVqR7gz50oKyCw5EkKVNTZ6DsZxo2gORlx5zdE2sFg4X9kWTYjMGC5R0j1wp4spyb6465_)** , I can tell you that we’ll be one step closer to doubling the number of Navy SEALS who have served in the U.S. Senate.

[**SEND A NAVY SEAL TO THE SENATE

clean_body: I’m starting to gain some traction in the race for Minnesota Senate, and so my political opponents are starting to go negative on me. | Fellow Conservative, As a former Navy SEAL , I’m used to being under attack. But the lies being told by my opponents who want to serve you in the US Senate is a new one for me. Something so sipmle that I’ve said on the campaign trail, or a position I’ve taken that my opponents may disagree with? It’s funny how an opponent can turn pretty much anything that comes out of a campaign into a flat out lie. Though I’ve been in the Minnesota Senate race for about a year now, I’m no household name by any means. But our campaign is beginning to attract the attention of voters around the state as I continue to win straw poll after straw poll (12 and counting now). Over the weekend we just won the Congressional District 3 straw poll by a wide margin! I knew I would be attacked at some point - but I naively believed it wouldn’t be so dirty or so intense. Personally, I can take the hits. I get it, my opponents see me as a threat. But here’s the deal: the Senate seat in Minnesota is too important to let petty grievances get in the way of defeating Democrats and taking back this Senate seat for the Republican Party. I know it may not be much to you, but , I can tell you that we’ll be one step closer to doubling the number of Navy SEALS who have served in the U.S. Senate. You may not know me - or even live in Minnesota, but here is what I can tell you today: I’m not running for the Senate to make contacts in D.C. that can get me a cushy job in the private sector like a lot of folks. I’m running because this country has given me every opportunity available and my service to Old Glory didn’t end when I left the military. Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
Team
The Constitution places the authority to run elections squarely with the states and Congress – NOT with the federal government.
But now, the President has issued another executive order imposing sweeping new federal control over election administration.
Make no mistake, Team, this is yet another unlawful attempt by this MAGA administration to sow confusion and distrust ahead of the fall midterm elections.
We're doing everything in our power to fight back and protect the right to vote , including:
➜ Registering eligible voters
➜ Putting election information directly in the hands of voters
➜ Combating election misinformation
➜ Advocating at every level to keep our elections truly free and fair
Team, it will take massive resources to stand up to this new executive order in time to make a difference before the midterm elections. We need your help ASAP: Will you chip in $35 or whatever you can afford right now? >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=042926_2&amount=35]

We will never stay silent when the right to vote is attacked, Team, including by a hostile administration in control of the federal government.

clean_body: This decision is a warning. | = Peter, Earlier today, the U.S. Supreme Court struck down Louisiana’s congressional map and narrowed a key protection in the Voting Rights Act. This decision will make it nearly impossible to challenge gerrymandered maps — and easier for Republican-controlled states to weaken voting power, lock in unfair advantages, and tilt the rules in their favor. But here’s what we know: The fight for fair elections does not begin and end in Washington. It depends on who holds power in the states. For too long, our party has failed to make the sustained investments needed to build real Democratic power at the state level. But for more than 40 years, EMILYs List has been doing exactly that: recruiting, training, supporting, and electing Democratic pro-choice women to state and local office across the country. | = Since our founding, we’ve helped elect more than 1,600 women to state and local office alone — victories that have flipped state legislatures, secured Democratic supermajorities, prevented Republican supermajorities, and strengthened the firewall against attacks on our rights and our democracy. Now, with the Supreme Court making it easier for Republican-led states to disenfranchise their voters, this work is more urgent than ever. Today’s decision is a warning: We cannot rely on the courts alone to protect our democracy. We have to win power in the states — because state legislatures draw maps, write election laws, and decide whether our democracy becomes more representative or more rigged. = If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue, your donation will go through immediately: = | = ---|--- = | = = | = Voting rights are fundamental to our democracy. I’m deeply dismayed by today’s U.S. Supreme Court ruling.
The decision guts Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act — which, since its passage in 1965, has helped make sure every single American, no matter their race, can exercise their constitutional right to vote.
While we still don’t know the full impacts of today’s ruling, we do know that when SCOTUS weakens the Voting Rights Act, states will all too often follow their lead with new voter suppression laws.
My fellow attorneys general and I will always fight for fair representation and equal rights under the law — and that fight just got even more important.

# [Tell ABC: "Don’t Let Trump Silence Jimmy Kimmel"](https://default.salsalabs.org/Te3f5ff24-f073-4cf1-a6de-f3ead4e6ea98/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9)

---
| | | _(Already took this action?[Click here for others](https://default.salsalabs.org/Tf051d9d0-37e8-4f41-8d1a-3425a1eff68b/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9). Want to unsubscribe? See link below)_ Donald and Melania Trump are [pressuring ABC to fire Jimmy Kimmel](https://default.salsalabs.org/T6399982b-50c1-4752-889a-aa61c6eb305e/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9) over a joke they didn't like. **Let's be clear: that's not accountability. That's an attempt to bully a network into silencing a critic.** On his show last week — before the dinner incident — Kimmel [joked](https://default.salsalabs.org/T7bd00e56-c66a-45e1-8e37-87c8e2d08b09/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9) that Melania had the "glow" of an "expectant widow," a line aimed at widely reported concerns about Donald Trump's age and health. It wasn't a threat. It wasn't a call to violence. It was satire — the kind late-night comedians have used for decades to hold powerful people up to the light. **[Tell ABC:"Don't Let Trump Silence Jimmy Kimmel"](https://default.salsalabs.org/Te585a8db-9cb9-49d3-993d-0340a32f5a26/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9)** The Trumps have every right to be offended. They can criticize Kimmel all they want. **But demanding he be fired — and backing that demand with the implied power of a federal government that regulates broadcast networks — crosses a dangerous line. That's not free speech. That's political pressure aimed at censorship.** If media companies start folding every time a powerful politician gets angry, then criticism becomes risky... and silence becomes the safer option. ABC must not cave.

**[Tell ABC:"Don't Let Trump Silence Jimmy Kimmel"](https://default.salsalabs.org/T390064e2-41f2-4347-a4ad-29463f27d3e6/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9)**

| | | | | | Dear Friends and Supporters,
Your ongoing support has meant the world to me, and I'm honored to serve the 28th District in the Pennsylvania State House. I'm writing today because the next election for my State House seat is closer than it may seem. **Early voting begins in less than six months, and I need your help once again.**
**** During my time in Harrisburg, I've been fighting for policies and values that will move Pennsylvania in the right direction. When I'm home in the district, my schedule is equally full connecting with community members and groups: constituent meetings, fire departments, veterans' groups, sportsmen's clubs, Eagle Scout ceremonies, school events, and more. _**I'm committed to earning every vote!**_
**The stakes in this election could not be higher**. Pennsylvania faces a defining choice: do we follow states like California and New York down the path of higher taxes, bigger government, and suffocating regulations? Or do we chart a course where pro-growth policies drive prosperity, protect individual freedom, and help families thrive?
**Our State House hangs by a single-seat margin**. After the 2024 election, the chamber stands at 102 Democrats to 101 Republicans. Of the 203 total seats, fewer than 20, mostly in suburban districts like ours, are competitive. Those races will determine the direction of Pennsylvania for years to come. Ours is one of the critical swing districts.
I would be grateful for your support as I work to get Pennsylvania on the right track. We have an upcoming fundraiser on **May 28th at Wildwood Country Club**(see details below). I would love to see you there! If you are unable to attend, any contribution will help us meet our goal and keep the fight going. We are also looking for volunteers to help get our message out. Reply to this email if you are able to help!

Patients who had no other options were seeing real results. Some are alive today because of this treatment.
And now it’s being blocked — while politicians pass the blame and distort the facts.
As a scientist, trust me when I say: This is what happens when ideology replaces evidence.
People get hurt. Families lose options. Lives are put at risk.
I’ve spent my career studying science, teaching it, and fighting for it — because when we follow the evidence, we save lives. And when we don’t, the consequences are devastating.
That’s exactly why I’m running for Congress. Because right now, we have leaders who are comfortable playing politics with public health — and we need leaders who will stand up and say: enough.
But taking on this kind of broken system requires real resources — and tonight is our end-of-month deadline.
We set a goal of raising $5,000 before midnight tomorrow because moments like this demand a response. If you believe public health decisions should be made by doctors and scientists — not politicians — I’m asking you to step up today: Chip in $10, 25, or whatever you can before midnight to help us hit our goal. >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jc_dsg-em?refcode=260429em-pancreatic]
DONATE NOW [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jc_dsg-em?refcode=260429em-pancreatic]
This campaign is about more than one race.
It’s about whether we accept a future where lifesaving treatments are blocked while politicians spin excuses — or whether we fight for something better.
I know which side I’m on. I hope you’ll stand with me.

name: Jamie Davis
subject: I can still hear his voice: “Dad, get me out.”
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY RESIST RECLAIM REBUILD PAC (WWW
body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-jamie [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-jamie]
August 8, 2009, is a date I will never forget.
Just days before his 19th birthday, my son Justin was out in the fields with us, doing what this family has done for over three generations—farming the Louisiana delta. A breakdown in our combine left corn spilled across the ground, and as we worked to recover it, Justin got too close. In an instant, his pant leg was caught, and the thresher pulled him in.
I can still hear his voice: “Dad, get me out.”
And there was nothing I could do.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-jamie [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-jamie]
Multiple miracles occurred that day: When it initially happened he wasn’t in pain because his nerves were pinched so tightly in the machine. Nor was he bleeding because he was caught so tight in there.
It took the jaws of life to tear apart that machine and when the metal finally gave way he let out a scream that I will never forget for the rest of my life.
The paramedics quickly sprang into action and he was airlifted to Jackson, Mississippi, where Doctors fought to save his leg, but the injury and infection from all the dirt and debris were too severe. Justin lost his leg from below the knee.
That day could have broken us. Instead, it showed me what makes Louisiana strong.
Neighbors, first responders from two parishes (what we call counties in Louisiana), and a doctor who wasn’t even on duty, Dr. Ron Gregg, a farmer himself and longtime family friend — showed up because that’s what rural communities do. They take care of each other. They don’t ask if it’s their job or jurisdiction. They just show up.
Today, Justin is 35. He runs our farm. He’s built a life, with a fiancée and a family of his own. He still hunts, fishes, and works the land — just with a prosthetic leg and the same determination that carried him through that day.
But the truth is, the kind of community that saved Justin is disappearing. Rural hospitals are closing. Doctors like Dr. Gregg—who live in our communities, who know our families—are harder to find. Too many of our kids feel like they have to leave home to build a future.
And my family, who first worked this Louisiana delta soil as slaves and sharecroppers, and now as farmers who own this land, have put too much blood into this soil for us to leave and go somewhere else.
I have to take a stand and fight for our way of life and it’s why I am proud to be the Democrat running for Senate in Louisiana.
If you believe in that fight, I’m asking you to stand with me today. A Democratic win here is the first step in taking our state back from the far-right whose policies of atomization and vicious corporatism are tearing our communities apart.
And mark my words, a win is possible, Democrats just won a deep red special election here by a landslide. The blue wave will wash over Louisiana and we will flip this seat but only if we fight for it. Will you please make a contribution of $50, $20, or even just $10 to help us in our fight to restore the Louisiana that we love so dearly. Thank you. Your support means more than you know.

disclaimer_text: Paid for by Mandela for Wisconsin
body:
I wanted to check in and let you know where things stand
| Darby, Mandela Barnes’ Campaign Manager here: We’re stepping up fundraising efforts. _I know, I know_ ... I doubt you’ve been eagerly checking your inbox for this! Trust me, I don’t love sending them either. If you’ll give me a minute, I want to explain why they matter for what we’re trying to build together. **Mandela Barnes has never taken a dime from corporate PACs.** So consistent grassroots donations to emails like these are the only way a 100% people-powered campaign can compete. **[If that’s all you need to hear to support Mandela’s campaign, you can chip in right now!](https://act.mandelabarnes.com/go/1212?c0=mb-em-fr-apr26.K8_u48&amount=15&refcode=MB_EM_FR_042926_B2_DarbyMemo&t=2&akid=6104%2E196590%2Eu-l5iq)** Since our campaign relies on you, I want to ensure you get an inside look at our campaign, here’s our latest state of the race memo for you: | **TO:** Interested Parties
**FROM:** Mandela Barnes for Governor
**MEMO:** **** The State of Wisconsin’s Toss-Up Governor’s Race **Mandela Barnes is running for Governor in Wisconsin on a platform centered on meeting this moment and building a better future by rejecting the dysfunction of the _Washington Way_ and uniting our state behind the _Wisconsin Way_ : where middle-class families can thrive, and we can build a better future for our children and grandchildren.** To be blunt: The full force of the radical MAGA machine is being put towards stopping us. Fueled in large part by corporate PACs and the same donors who put Donald Trump back in the White House. Billionaire donors are going all-in against us. We are in the middle of a tough fight. _**About Mandela:**_ Mandela Barnes grew up in Milwaukee. Raised by a public school teacher mother and a father who worked third shift at the local General Motors plant, who instilled him with **a deep commitment to hard work and public service.** Mandela practiced those values when he was elected to the Wisconsin State Assembly at just 25 years old. He quickly became a legislative champion for the environment, the economy, racial justice, and healthcare, before helping to kick Scott Walker out of office to become the nation's youngest — and Wisconsin's first Black — Lieutenant Governor. After a hard-fought U.S. Senate race where tens of millions of dollars in dark money defeated him by just a single point, **Mandela is now running for Governor to meet a critical moment for his state.** With family farmers being squeezed by tariffs, healthcare costs rising, and the devastating chaos from Washington under Trump threatening working people, Mandela refuses to stand idly by. He has the proven public service record and personal dedication necessary to cut through the division and ensure no Wisconsin family is ever just one emergency away from financial disaster. _**Tomorrow's deadline:**_ After Thursday at midnight, our campaign has to review how much money we’ve raised – and from how many donors. We’ll have to make tough decisions about our budget, because the only way to compete with right-wing dark money is to use every cent efficiently. It’s critical that we raise enough to fund the most competitive campaign operation possible. _**Where you come in:**_ We’re counting on grassroots donors to harness people power to give us the resources to fight back. **The bottom line: The only way we’ll be able to raise the funds to run a competitive campaign is with your help, .**
---
If we’re going to elect Mandela Barnes this November and bring generational change to Wisconsin, we need you.
**[Please, can you give $15 or any amount you’re able to towards Mandela’s campaign today?](https://act.mandelabarnes.com/go/1212?c0=mb-em-fr-apr26.K8_u48&amount=15&refcode=MB_EM_FR_042926_B2_DarbyMemo&t=3&akid=6104%2E196590%2Eu-l5iq)**

name: Eric H. Holder, Jr.
subject: BREAKING: Supreme Court just effectively gutted the Voting Rights Act
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY THE NATIONAL REDISTRICTING ACTION FUND
body:
We’ve been preparing for this devastating ruling, and we’re ready to fight back.
|
---

Peter,
**In effectively gutting Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act, the Court today ensures that it will be remembered as one of the most destructive and deeply irresponsible Courts in the history of our nation. **
Time and again, in a variety of areas, this Court’s packed, radical majority has shown open hostility to long-held precedents that protect the rights of the American people, and a blatant disregard for facts that do not fit the ideological outcome they prefer. In this instance, by reversing precedent set less than three years ago—by this very same Court—the majority has taken its already extreme predilections to new lows.
Through judicial fiat, the Roberts Court has aimed to create a system where billionaires and corporations can more easily buy elections while American citizens, particularly people of color, and specifically black people, are forced to navigate increasingly difficult obstacles that aim to suppress their vote: from inappropriate voter purges to polling location closures and, now, essentially unfettered gerrymandering. It is an approach that is untethered, not only from the American founding ideals, but also from any semblance of legal and judicial norms.
**It should not be lost on anyone that the Roberts court makes this decision at a time when Republican leaders across the country are foaming at the mouth to draw the American people out of a meaningful say in our elections. They want to retain illegitimately obtained power through the use of, among other things, now Supreme Court sanctioned racial and partisan gerrymandering.**
This status quo must change.
Moving forward, the remedy to this out-of-control, deeply ideological Court must be a renewed commitment by the American people—and those who represent them—to pass new, durable voting rights legislation as well as reforms to our judicial system, so that the Supreme Court is no longer held captive by a minority ideology that acts solely in the best interest of those who adhere to it.
In solidarity,
Eric H. Holder, Jr.
82nd Attorney General of the United States

The reality? **We’re right in the thick of it.** Once Primary Day wraps up 20 days from today, all eyes will be on this campaign. Concerned citizens [crowding](https://substack.com/redirect/4afc15c5-6267-4b8b-b800-a900be137def?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) into a town hall to protest a proposed data center in El Paso, Texas. Suburban homeowners [shouting down](https://substack.com/redirect/4eb77139-8d11-4151-88b7-4fe19f142c41?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) pro-data center politicians in Festus, Missouri. Teenagers and their parents [swamping](https://substack.com/redirect/6bee31da-d7d5-49a9-951b-12f667e60a27?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a local zoning meeting to demand an end to data center construction in DeKalb County, Georgia. Conservative farmers rising up to [block](https://substack.com/redirect/02c358a5-e5e4-4fd9-a7a9-5d48d051b9f4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a data center in Howell Township, Michigan.
The grassroots resistance to AI data centers that is springing up in communities across the country outlines the kind of multiracial working-class coalition many of us on the Left have always dreamed of--a diverse, nonpartisan, top-bottom movement against Big Tech billionaires that has the potential to reshape American politics in incredibly positive ways.
[Subscribed](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9hYXJvbnJlZ3VuYmVyZy5zdWJzdGFjay5jb20vYWNjb3VudCIsInAiOjE5NTg5MTk4NCwicyI6NDk4MTE3MCwiZiI6dHJ1ZSwidSI6OTA1MDExOTIsImlhdCI6MTc3NzQ4ODM2NSwiZXhwIjoyMDkzMDY0MzY1LCJpc3MiOiJwdWItMCIsInN1YiI6ImxpbmstcmVkaXJlY3QifQ.124bS_bUpIatn2SwHq6fGJuFCfOLJ9ZhpfpxPvbZnWg?)
The most immediate, short-term policy demand driving this local organizing is a moratorium on new data centers. There are different versions of this policy: Senator Bernie Sanders and Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez have introduced a [national moratorium](https://substack.com/redirect/1af55188-a66c-4eef-8d6d-e80c9388d537?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg); statewide moratoria have been proposed in at least [twelve states](https://substack.com/redirect/c3de2c9d-9627-4200-b59f-eda5c391aac4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) (and one passed in Maine, though the legislation was [vetoed](https://substack.com/redirect/47fdc4d8-6929-4537-832d-28c8e9b0b3c8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by Governor Janet Mills); and [dozens](https://substack.com/redirect/03675a16-35c3-4b38-9f9c-bd3c38173776?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of cities, towns, and counties have already enacted such laws.
This pushback has drawn its own pushback. In a recent _Jacobin_ [essay](https://substack.com/redirect/c9307fad-c39f-4a7b-a397-57a8de47c3f0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), Holly Buck argues that "a moratorium on AI data centers is a terrible idea" that "poses serious equity concerns." Such a pause, she writes, "is not a substitute for actual AI governance."
This argument--and Buck, of course, is far from the only person making it--seems to misunderstand the thrust of the data center moratorium effort, which is to stall the breakneck development of these projects _so that we can enact "actual AI governance_._"_ Buck complains that organizations supporting "data center blocking efforts should put their attention towards a broader set of solutions"--which is exactly what they have been doing. My organization, Public Citizen, developed a comprehensive suite of [actionable steps](https://substack.com/redirect/6cc76e90-ac54-4225-a124-c5d67ba1ad2b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to rein in Big Tech and make sure consumers, workers, and the climate are protected from the data center buildout. And we're not alone; other organizations, like the NAACP, have also released [guiding principles](https://substack.com/redirect/046476fe-af70-4b9c-b521-961fd50d9b96?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for equitable data center development.
The problem is not that we don't have policy solutions to this crisis. The problem is that Big Tech's private (and [unpopular](https://substack.com/redirect/91c697d0-1fa0-49ac-9a28-3d1124fafb7f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)) investment in data centers is moving at an astounding pace, and we don't have the time or leverage to establish the regulatory framework necessary to make this system work for the public. In the words of [Alex Bores](https://substack.com/redirect/6cc4dd1d-da06-4658-b50c-22712b0c3984?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), a candidate for Congress who worked in Big Tech and whom tech billionaires have spent millions of dollars attacking because of his support for AI regulation, moratoria proposals
> are setting the terms of the debate, which is: Why are we going forward with this until we've done the real work? ... If I could wave a magic wand and pass any bill I want, it wouldn't be the moratorium. It would be the regulations that the moratorium is calling for. But putting that as a negotiating tactic, I think, is meeting the moment.
The criticism that the push for a data center moratorium fails to resolve every issue of "actual AI governance" seems to rest on the idea that there is a magic wand we could wave to pass any bill we want. But there is no magic wand. And though moratorium opponents like Buck say that "the people should be driving this discussion, not companies like OpenAI," they never offer alternative suggestions for how the people could overcome the Big Tech billionaires that are [putting](https://substack.com/redirect/4948fb5a-399b-408e-a976-3e62c19b920c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) hundreds of millions of dollars into super PACs to block any attempts at real regulation. The passage of data center moratoria is--as far as I can tell, and as far as anyone else out there seems to be able to tell--essentially the only tool available to us that could exert meaningful leverage over these companies.
This leverage stems in part from the fact that Big Tech really wants to build their hyperscalers here in the United States. Buck asserts that these companies would respond to a moratorium by simply offshoring their data centers. But developing countries do not have the energy and grid infrastructure to support these projects, absent absolutely massive investments by Big Tech. What's more, offshore hyperscalers would [respond](https://substack.com/redirect/b2f2a162-d2a8-4846-88d0-6209acad7f6d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to queries significantly more slowly than domestic ones, further compounding costs, particularly for products that are highly interactive. Big Tech will go to great lengths to avoid these problems. (As an aside, Buck also warns from an equity perspective that we should be "wary of proposals that would send burdens elsewhere." But this is tantamount to saying, "You must let the ruling class hurt you, because otherwise they might hurt someone less privileged than you." It's essentially an argument corporations could make against any jurisdiction in the U.S. passing any pro-social regulation at all--an extremely convenient paradigm for the forces of capital.)
Securing this leverage is clearly necessary to rein in Big Tech's dangerous practices, which are as diverse as the constituencies mobilizing to oppose them. Many data center opponents are motivated by the impact of these projects on energy costs--electricity prices in some data center-dense areas have surged [over 250 percent](https://substack.com/redirect/75fc6cc8-3697-4620-8d86-2d2d416383a0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in recent years, and in 2024 customers of PJM [paid $4.3 billion](https://substack.com/redirect/aab2f11e-a4bd-4877-88ef-ffcec6754182?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) more in electricity costs to cover data centers' new transmission infrastructure. Others rightly fear the environmental and climate harms of this buildout--data centers' energy demand is [actively extending](https://substack.com/redirect/cfd3eeff-582a-4a44-89c2-aeba6a7b02d6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the life of dirty coal plants and driving a massive expansion of new gas-fired power plants. Some harbor deeper concerns over the dangers this technology poses to our society, and the way that AI currently serves powerful capitalist interests.
From [discrimination](https://substack.com/redirect/4d302f03-b76f-4bc5-bb00-a70379829d46?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in facial recognition systems, to [disastrous attempts](https://substack.com/redirect/c91b9cd6-b50c-4117-81c3-979e4559c06f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to integrate AI chatbots into public schools, to RealPage's algorithmic [facilitation](https://substack.com/redirect/facf48e5-232e-4e28-8b6f-41579b62188a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of rental price-fixing, to Amazon's AI-supported [surveillance](https://substack.com/redirect/09c3a315-5251-465a-b8de-80d70f146c19?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of warehouse workers, to the use of AI to [justify](https://substack.com/redirect/37887f8f-2001-46bf-8784-a288079e202a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) benefit cuts and Medicaid coverage denials to low-income people, to the increasingly prevalent [algorithmic wage exploitation](https://substack.com/redirect/aff66b50-440f-45c1-b3d6-b1f2f5279d24?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of gig workers, to the growth of [dystopian state surveillance](https://substack.com/redirect/ea1bcabc-171b-4ef4-a481-34f3fbdbc49d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), to the fact that I can't ever find a goddamned customer service phone number anymore because they've all been replaced by AI chatbots, the actual evidence is clear that AI is not liberating us as individuals but rather concentrating power in the hands of those who already have far too much control over our lives.
Some moratorium opponents have framed the diversity of these coalitions as a deficit. As Buck wrote, "Part of why the moratorium push is such a dead end is because the disparate right-left coalitions that have emerged around stopping data centers have different interests when it comes to other issues." But building coalitions among constituencies with "different interests when it comes to other issues" is the entire work of politics, and always has been. Talk to any on-the-ground organizers, and they will tell you that it is actually the diversity of data center opponents that makes this issue so politically potent.
I asked a colleague of mine, Kamil Cook, who has been supporting data center campaigns in Texas, to share some reflections on this organizing. "There are certainly political contradictions that some working class groups are struggling through," he told me.
> But I've seen how these fights are forcing communities to reckon with how power functions in places like rural Texas. They're helping people realize that their politicians do not serve them and the only way that they can protect their community is by standing together and figuring out their own solutions. I've worked with some incredibly conservative Texans and many of them have referenced Bernie's policies on data centers and AI. Imagine if there was a real political current that was articulating their concerns?"
Ben Inskeep, another organizer who's been supporting these fights in Indiana, [put it this way](https://substack.com/redirect/9a63d63e-ae74-4c53-8070-593e3d8effdb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg): "People from all walks of life are waking up to the broken system we have where both parties are exploiting us. Not a 'dead end.' An incredible opportunity for class consciousness!
We should __ think of this fight as an opportunity. A genuinely nationwide coalition has organically formed in opposition to the greed and avarice of an industry that is endangering our democracy, undermining our labor, and enshittifying every aspect of our lives. That coalition has settled, for completely sound strategic reasons, on demands for national, state, and local moratoria on AI data centers. The Left should be uniformly on its side.

Fellow Patriot,

I just got back from a meeting with Kurt Alme, the Republican candidate for U.S. Senate in Montana.

_I want to tell you about him._

Kurt is a Montana native, born and raised across the Treasure State. He's spent almost his entire career in public service. As U.S. Attorney, nominated by President Trump and unanimously confirmed by the Senate, he went after the violent criminals, drug cartels, and traffickers that were destroying Montana communities. He didn't just talk about fighting crime. He prosecuted more defendants than any year in the last two decades.

Before that, he cut Montana's top income tax rate as Director of the Montana Department of Revenue. As Budget Director for Governor Gianforte, he reduced spending, cut taxes, and helped make Montana debt-free.

This is a man with a real record of results.

But what struck me sitting across from Kurt wasn't just his resume. It was his conviction.

He believes in the same things we do. Secure borders. Safe communities. Fiscal responsibility. Standing with President Trump to put America First. And protecting a Montana way of life that is worth fighting for.

**The Left knows Montana is a battleground. They are going to pour money into this race._They have already started building their operation_.**

Kurt is ready to fight. But he needs resources to do it.

**[Will you make a donation to Kurt Alme's campaign today? Your contribution, whatever you can give, will help him build the kind of campaign that can win in November and keep this Senate seat in Republican hands.](http://links.ourdefenseofamerica.com/u/click?_t=aa3ef0db03454a26b650c9ca7e919386&_m=677cf9842f9940c28bb4c70ae3b8be48&_e=TLIqb0_aH9pCIl9DfBjKwbMydPB2g7EDvvXyMnW1ZZeUCp--6X0NrgjAKSvHXwut3um06LSlUw5V_ql3I94Yh-u9b4KYZi8bOL6Cnp0hUXNsEMWu9X_TeaEC8bo9Klj_0ryld8T4fYR3YcwkgUPf1jicelceDRWyXx22rNxrR2RBix66F52f08s4iduPmHUME2a1B7F6M2LjgPkYDWiDEViJg7vwoz53-0jvFth3djt2TEJn06P_WSRJYTeLSLEEQRb3rosYKpSeWwr9rNSMBrwY-aDY-pSw0yKtShUYxJWZrrJ0VPYe-BCDorFIKS48QbfEO2F83nmch9R468-767rXYbaf71tpBNIG9FKtei56dpP1578ZZt1m-k-SbzIeYZ0GlZk4TO6keDR60icKnWtgTD2U9HAOGBh6P25WIlvGiTCZ8YHwuZ-2n5dTcZhZW9nRoxZZOXTatQUaorEP5l6l7yP9bBwadtrf2p7t0LEq1hq4YMQIma1uMe0LbOKtLD2pvEaXs5CYGj1Tj6AgpKpjsu2mf9nPQDoPa55y6CMN4ruf2GtD5y3jyt1jgBvHARPIXkq826P-gbX_BySTbw0zJ8967wCJ_5PcoaPSVvVnJ3qIBZ07VyU0nISWO0O1wlRBqdejc84qcwmoPmp8qMDklUAaEaRcnpm397GpwYLUelZSx9Z1mFHnlyHCK0SWavvlyyRlbpQ0Tn1ijqrOyg%3D%3D)**

The lobbying blueprint behind Colorado’s parental rights erosion
| | | | [](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
---
**PRESENTED BY[ROCKYMOUNTAINVOICE.COM](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
| | Hey friends,
After announcing Nick Shirley as our first Freedom Festival speaker, we’ve got another major name dropping today... but you have to be on our [priority list](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) to hear it first! Let’s just say—you’ve probably seen him late at night, and he’s not exactly known for holding back. Stay tuned 👀 [And get your tickets here!](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
Want your full news breakdown? Listen to the Mountain Minute podcast [here](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), or watch on [YouTube](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) or [Rumble](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.). And don't miss our deep-dive video the LITERAL blueprint the left is using to [push gender policy at the Capitol](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.). Here is a summary of today's top stories:

**🏛️ Under the Golden Dome...** Lawmakers are advancing a bill that could lock in [decades-long charges on Xcel customer bills](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) to cover power plant costs, while prison overcrowding is fueling debate as Democrats push [increased inmate releases](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) instead of funding new capacity. Flags are being raised as a series of recent bills affecting parental rights, school policies, and custody law [mirror a 2019 "activist" playbook](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.).
**🏔️ Here in Colorado...** A [Satanic Temple student won a religious exemption](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) from a school digital monitoring system, while the Colorado Supreme Court [limited the reach of consumer protections](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) in insurance disputes. A judge [declined to step aside in the Tina Peters case](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), as concerns also surface over [China-linked funding](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) tied to environmental groups and state politics.
**🇺🇸 On the National Stage...** Republicans face warnings of [midterm voter complacency](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) amid economic frustration and shifting turnout dynamics without Trump on the ballot, while prosecutors allege the [Southern Poverty Law Center funded operatives within extremist groups](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), raising questions about its use of donor funds.
This is your Mountain Minute for Wednesday, April 29, 2026.
– Team RMV
---
|
---
**TODAY'S TOP STORIES**
**[The lobbying blueprint behind Colorado’s parental rights erosion](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY SHAINA COLE, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
In 2019, a team of lawyers at one of the world’s largest firms produced a document explaining, in precise detail, how to change the law around children and gender without the public knowing it was happening.
That document is now a lens through which Colorado’s last three legislative sessions make a different kind of sense.
Formally titled “[Only Adults? Good Practices in Legal Gender Recognition for Youth](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.),” the 65-page report was produced pro bono by Dentons — the world’s largest law firm by attorney headcount — along with the Thomson Reuters Foundation and [IGLYO](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), the International Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Transgender, Queer and Intersex Youth & Student Organisation. Released during Transgender Awareness Week, it came with standard disclaimers from both institutional partners that it didn’t reflect their views. One UK contributor went unnamed.

**[Judge Barrett refuses to step aside in Peters case, defends sentencing math](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY JEN SCHUMANN, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* **Judge denies recusal request in Tina Peters case:** Judge Matthew Barrett rejected the motion to disqualify himself, ruling that none of the claims met the legal standard for bias even when accepting the defense’s assertions as true.
* **Dispute centers on sentencing and legal interpretation:** The defense argued Barrett misrepresented the sentence length by running terms consecutively, while the judge maintained each sentence fell within statutory ranges and complied with the law.
* **Appeal process moves forward amid procedural questions:** With recusal resolved, the court must rule on bond within a 48-hour window, as broader constitutional challenges and appellate review—including claims about trial fairness—continue to develop.

**[Energy Foundation China Has Been Generous to Those Dealing in Colorado Politics](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [COLORADO ACCOUNTABILITY PROJECT](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* **China-linked foundation tied to Colorado political ecosystem:** Energy Foundation China—though headquartered in San Francisco—is described as having strong ties to Beijing and the Chinese government while funding organizations involved in Colorado policy.
* **Significant funding flows to environmental nonprofits:** The group has provided financial support to multiple environmental and policy-focused nonprofits operating in Colorado, highlighting the scale of its influence within the state.
* **Concerns raised over influence on governance and policy:** The commentary points to broader questions about how outside funding may shape state decisions, alongside criticism of legislation that shifts authority from elected officials to appointed boards with taxing power.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**

**ONLY ON ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE ⤵️ **
**[The empty pail: The first step up the mountain](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** **BY DRAKE HUNTER | COMMENTARY | APRIL 27** _“Jack and Jill went up the hill to fetch a pail of water...” Continuing with last devotion’s rhyme, we often remember the fall... but rarely ask the deeper question: What if they made it to the top... but never learned how to draw from the well? Because in the life of following Jesus, the issue is not whether we’ve started the climb—it’s whether we are being formed and becoming who we need to be as we go to do what God needs us to do._
**[If the state can take property without a conviction, no property is safe](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)****BY REP. KEN DEGRAAF | COMMENTARY | APRIL 27** _Civil asset forfeiture began as a narrow exception in colonial maritime law, not as a general tool of domestic policing. In those early admiralty cases, the government often had jurisdiction over the ship or cargo, but not over the owner. The vessel might be in port, but the owner could be overseas, unknown, or beyond the reach of the court. In that circumstance, proceeding against the property itself—an action in rem—was often the only practical way to enforce customs law.___
**[Trump’s DOJ joins xAI suit against Colorado AI law as Weiser agrees to halt enforcement](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)****BY SHAINA COLE | STATE | APRIL 27** _The Colorado attorney general agreed last week to stop enforcing the state’s landmark artificial intelligence law. Not because a court told him to. Because he agreed to it himself. That voluntary freeze, formalized in a joint filing with plaintiff xAI LLC, came the same afternoon the U.S. Department of Justice moved to join the lawsuit challenging SB24-205 — Colorado’s AI consumer protection law set to take effect June 30._ __

name: Team Taylor
subject: Chris is endorsing Pedro Colón for Wisconsin Supreme Court
body:
Check out what she had to say >>
#
It's Team Taylor reaching out to share that Justice-elect Chris Taylor is enthusiastically endorsing Judge Pedro Colón for the open seat on the Wisconsin Supreme Court!
[](https://act.leftnet.org/go/22700?source=em20260429-1617&t=1&akid=1617%2E2118727%2EK4lE7V)
In announcing her endorsement, Chris said:
"Pedro Colón is exactly the kind of justice Wisconsin needs on its Supreme Court," said Justice-elect Taylor. "His depth of judicial and life experience would be a welcome and important perspective to the court. Over his 15 years on the bench, he has proven to be a fair and impartial judge who treats everyone that comes before his court with dignity and respect. I have seen his work up close. I know his record. And I know he has the experience, the judgment, and the steady temperament the people of Wisconsin deserve on their highest court. I’m proud to endorse my friend, Pedro Colón and, next spring, I hope the voters of our state send him to serve with me on the Wisconsin Supreme Court.”
Chris has seen Pedro's work up close, she knows his judgement, and she knows the steady temperament he would bring to the bench that the people of Wisconsin deserve on their Supreme Court.
As you know, Supreme Court elections are important in Wisconsin, and we have the chance to REPLACE a far-right justice with a proven leader who will join Chris in actually representing Wisconsin values.
**[We know this election feels far away, but Pedro is hoping to receive your grassroots endorsement today in order to build a strong coalition against the right wing billionaires. No contribution necessary: will you give Judge Pedro Colón your endorsement today?](https://act.leftnet.org/go/22700?source=em20260429-1617&t=2&akid=1617%2E2118727%2EK4lE7V)**

| | In its decision in Louisiana v. Callais, the U.S. Supreme Court gutted the core requirement of the Voting Rights Act to protect minority opportunity districts. The Court overturned decades of precedent and undercut a core victory of the Civil Rights Movement.
With this ruling, the Court has opened the door to diluting Black, Latino, AANHPI, Native American, and Alaska Native representation across the country, especially in the South, where Republicans have made clear they want to split the voting power of minority communities.
While the Supreme Court’s decision is a gut punch, make no mistake: Democrats remain undeterred and will fight tooth and nail to ensure the voices of all Americans will be heard in November and in every election that follows. We must organize, mobilize, and remain vigilant in defending the right to vote. The fight against racial gerrymandering is now more urgent than ever, and the hard-won right to vote must be protected for all Americans. This moment calls for immediate action: stay engaged, support voting rights advocacy, and hold elected leaders accountable for restoring fair maps and fair elections.

We will be joined by: Davante Lewis, Louisiana Public Service Commissioner (District 3); Cliff Albright, Co-founder of Black Voters Matter Fund; and Charles Taylor, Executive Director of the NAACP Mississippi State Conference.

| |
_Republican legislatures and governors now have to decide whether to undermine the power of Black, Latino, AANHPI, and Native American voters in their states_ Today, in its decision in _Louisiana v. Callais_ , the U.S. Supreme Court gutted the core requirement of the Voting Rights Act to protect minority opportunity districts. The Court overturned decades of precedent and undercut a core victory of the Civil Rights Movement. With this ruling, the Court has opened the door to diluting Black, Latino, AANHPI, and Native American representation across the country, especially in the South, where Republicans have made clear they want to split the voting power of minority communities.In September, Trump’s DOJ explicitly [asked](https://collegedems.us12.list-manage.com/track/click?u=b3a52587106e5f265f227782b&id=ea5ca567a3&e=d6c5c7d7ec) the Court to allow Republican legislators to weaken, and in some cases eliminate, the voting power of communities of color. The administration’s request — and today’s decision — go hand in hand with Trump and Republicans’ plot to rig congressional maps to dilute the voting power of Black and Latino voters ahead of the 2026 midterm elections. Today’s decision gives Republican legislatures and governors the power to undermine the power of Black, Latino, AANHPI, and Native American voters in their states — and where they choose to, Democrats will push back all across the country, every step of the way._In response,**DNC Chair Ken Martin released the following statement:**_ “Today is a dark day for America — the Supreme Court just rolled back the clock on the Civil Rights Movement. The GOP-captured Supreme Court just effectively killed Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act, a major step back in the fight for racial justice and fair representation. While today’s decision is a gut punch, make no mistake: Democrats will fight tooth and nail to ensure the voices of all Americans will be heard in November and in every election that follows.”

subject: What we’re doing right now matters
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Pramila for Congress
body:
Last Friday my campaign held our annual Build Our America luncheon here in Seattle.
# [](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/892?refcode=em20260429-6187-footer&t=1&akid=6187%2E420207%2ERHSJ2A)
Peter,
Last Friday my campaign held our annual Build Our America luncheon here in Seattle, and the energy in the room was _electric!_
[](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20260429-1.l63vz1&refcode=em20260429-6187&t=2&akid=6187%2E420207%2ERHSJ2A)
This year, we came together to raise money for our progressive movement and talk about what we can do to resist authoritarianism in our own communities. We heard from outstanding, inspiring speakers who showed how they’re taking action:.
**Congresswoman Delia Ramirez** was on the front lines of the resistance when ICE and CBP came to Chicago in full force, and she told us about her work building coalitions across movements and communities as she pushes forward in the fight for immigrant justice and economic justice.
**King County Councilwoman Teresa Mosqueda** spoke about the first in the nation resolution she helped pass right here in King County that calls for no more funding for ICE and CBP without real reforms—a resolution that originated in the Resistance Lab!
**Common Power Executive Director Charles Douglas** spoke about the opportunity to build a strong, effective, nonviolent resistance movement in this moment—one that demands a new kind of bold, progressive leadership not just in blue districts like Seattle’s, but across the entire country.
Our speakers showed what it means to fight for the most vulnerable, and I’m so grateful they joined us last Friday.

body:
We're enjoying traveling around beautiful Eastern Washington.

| | | | | |
---
|
---
| |
# Fair & parade season is getting started!
---
| |
One of the best parts of running for Congress is traveling around Eastern Washington to meet people and enjoy the local community events that showcase the many wonderful aspects of this area.Last weekend Team Baumgartner was in Asotin for the parade and fair. Thank you to the Asotin County GOP for supporting our efforts! We also had fun stopping by St John for the annual Community Fair, with its “Fields of Fun” theme!There will be many more great events over these coming months, and our team plans to attend a lot of them. If you’re interested in joining us for a couple of hours to walk in a parade or wave signs, please send a note back or sign up below and we will make sure to keep you updated about what is coming up!
---
| | | | | | | | | | |
---
| |
---
| |
# Washington Federation of Republican Women’s Spring Meeting
---
| | Thank you to the Washington State Republican Women for including my wife Eleanor as their lunch keynote speaker for their spring Board of Directors meeting in Spokane.
Eleanor had a great time visiting with many of our longstanding friends - as well as meeting some new ones - and speaking on “Celebrating 250: An Immigrant’s Top Ten of Life in America”. (The highlights included everything from self-reliance and respect for our military and veterans, to clothes dryers, in case you were wondering!)
---
|
---
| | _Eleanor with Ponderosa Republican Women’s Club members_
---
| |
# Lincoln Day in Stevens County
---
| | Thank you to the Stevens County GOP for the warm welcome and a great event in Colville! We’re grateful for all the hard work done to support candidates and to celebrate and promote our American values.

---
|
---
| | _Stevens County Lincoln Day Dinner 2026_
---

# Getting Involved!

Callais_****. 1** [](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm39uDKkapQVnT18L0ER7M9FmfThJYf2BhJjru3yZF27_GRU2101eC8Z200UVf-KFAj8BezrR8iaV3K7RSqbToAwMn4-_zs7KVtM-u5iV3MAHcKQ2uM2rO6yeN8-xFQnl29ahVqVaTsygxH28fcenFZRn1-hpwpu8wZakV_lnLEyXKhQuY4W5ri_jlOjveWsjQgMCGM8eSra3laphc7ar3xTZ-roYQE6fwngp5D2uhPlVIYV1xBxgYg8U57nfxUoImam2ixBaVIs202bqzc-NhklKpfQcjR3KW-3phi9Sj6iPF3kCpBhRm_I1hLGHuGdexIXDkSgvUxR8Ej5LNIBw1e2MmmLSkJXwroBbfakMQqvDuA/4q7/WdTUnT9FTNS8zqL7sZSHyA/h0/h001.s8Hlb3-6DFLUwbfoREgbiM-SSqKl3t5PmsltikEKZIc) The 6-3 decision guts what’s left of the Voting Rights Act, eliminating Louisiana’s second majority-Black district and attacking the right to vote for Black and Brown voters. **And just in time for the midterms, the decision tips the scales for Republicans by blessing partisan, racial gerrymandering in red states across the country.** The MAGA justices think they can tell us who counts and whose voices matter with zero accountability. But the Constitution doesn’t belong to them or their power-hungry extremist buddies—it belongs to us. [**Enough is enough. clean_body: The MAGA Supreme Court just stole more power from voters and communities. | | Peter, It’s pretty clear that our political system isn’t working for We the People—the everyday voters, working families, and communities of this country. And today, the Supreme Court has stripped even more power from working people with their breaking decision in Louisiana v. Callais. 1 The 6-3 decision guts what’s left of the Voting Rights Act, eliminating Louisiana’s second majority-Black district and attacking the right to vote for Black and Brown voters. And just in time for the midterms, the decision tips the scales for Republicans by blessing partisan, racial gerrymandering in red states across the country. The MAGA justices think they can tell us who counts and whose voices matter with zero accountability. But the Constitution doesn’t belong to them or their power-hungry extremist buddies—it belongs to us. Wages are falling behind ever-rising costs. Communities are being targeted by secretive police forces. Billionaires are pouring record money into manipulating our elections. Worst of all, the MAGA Supreme Court has done enormous damage to our democracy. As they strip our rights away, they give their extreme right-wing backers and wealthy corporate interests more power and control. Louisiana v. Callaisfollows the exact same pattern—less power for us, more control for the wealthy and powerful. The corrupt, bought-and-paid-for Supreme Court have yet again announced that they’re siding with their MAGA handlers.This is a crisis. We need court reforms to restore power to the people immediately. Power keeps moving upward—away from voters, working families, and communities, and toward the wealthy, powerful interests, and unaccountable institutions. We have to break the cycle. Thank you for fighting for a just system, Ken’Travius Coleman United for Democracy 1 Paid for by United for Democracy. | | Sent via . body:
We discovered something dark that no one is talking about. If we don’t get the word out about this we are going to be in store for a dire awakening.
| | | | | [](https://yfq78zhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001u3RbwrMECFglvU8UGcMQoZg_RNQyQoUVuUt03dgzHhrvUjKfUaJR5Zkxvd7hFFwAInS20jWvTt8D0PDz77KRMmdABQ3pAh-R0yNeQextqSeG_AK_LU7SVrTZnDmdumcwWeNLy7uk5oWSSS_30HtumHF_OnlrzbtkE14iLtT9IuLcAAjXnAoxcJXRkVsQgUZjPSXDUG-NWPTJyzbA3u81ObNZC0c3azh8&c=KzwlLuz3160UEdVpSNDlPyG1fU683bwxQJOy_nptkVpwuPWutGyWhg==&ch=Cv_z_-d26l9PS_Nstl_DPO7P4WmykDfTOHPveAHnXgMGa64aWZcCPw==)

Peter,
Why? That's the question on people's minds as the Trump Administration moves to seize voter record in states across the country - at least eight according to bombshell reporting from Reuters.
We know the answer. And it's terrifying:
In 2021, a dark money group called True the Vote attempted to challenge more than 364,000 Georgia voters just before the Senate runoff election -- the election that handed Democrats two seats and control of the Senate. Their targets? Young voters and Black voters were twice as likely to be challenged. The same voters who flipped Georgia in 2020.
---
| [](https://yfq78zhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001u3RbwrMECFglvU8UGcMQoZg_RNQyQoUVuUt03dgzHhrvUjKfUaJR5Zkxvd7hFFwAInS20jWvTt8D0PDz77KRMmdABQ3pAh-R0yNeQextqSeG_AK_LU7SVrTZnDmdumcwWeNLy7uk5oWSSS_30HtumHF_OnlrzbtkE14iLtT9IuLcAAjXnAoxcJXRkVsQgUZjPSXDUG-NWPTJyzbA3u81OfWyv0XdBxLu&c=KzwlLuz3160UEdVpSNDlPyG1fU683bwxQJOy_nptkVpwuPWutGyWhg==&ch=Cv_z_-d26l9PS_Nstl_DPO7P4WmykDfTOHPveAHnXgMGa64aWZcCPw==)

A federal judge later found that True the Vote's data "utterly lacked credibility" and that its approach "verged on reckless." But here's the thing about dark money operations: getting caught doesn't stop them. It just sends them back to find better data. Official government voter records are better data.
That's what MAGA is collecting right now, state by state -- the raw material for a voter suppression operation that makes 2021 look like a dry run.
And True the Vote doesn't operate alone. It sits inside the same vast dark money web connected to Leonard Leo -- the man who packed the Supreme Court, the man whose network has spent hundreds of millions capturing courts at every level, the man behind the system that gave Donald Trump criminal immunity.
We know how this sounds. We wish it were a conspiracy theory. It isn't. This is happening in real time, in plain sight, with federal resources behind it. Here's what stops them: State Supreme Courts.
Most election cases don't end up in front of Trump's hand-picked federal judges. They end up in front of state Supreme Courts -- courts whose justices are chosen by voters, not by presidents. That's why Leo's network has spent millions targeting those courts.
And that's why Defend Our Courts exists. We're the counter to MAGA's sinister dark money machine that is currently trying to buy our courts and steal elections. We beat them in Pennsylvania. We beat them in Wisconsin. And now: Georgia votes on May 19th.
A win in Georgia puts us on the path to flipping that court before the 2028 presidential election, before the next wave of voter suppression schemes lands in front of a judge.

clean_body: We discovered something dark that no one is talking about. If we don’t get the word out about this we are going to be in store for a dire awakening. | | | | | == | Peter, Why? That's the question on people's minds as the Trump Administration moves to seize voter record in states across the country - at least eight according to bombshell reporting from Reuters. We know the answer. And it's terrifying: In 2021, a dark money group called True the Vote attempted to challenge more than 364,000 Georgia voters just before the Senate runoff election -- the election that handed Democrats two seats and control of the Senate. Their targets? Young voters and Black voters were twice as likely to be challenged. The same voters who flipped Georgia in 2020. | == A federal judge later found that True the Vote's data "utterly lacked credibility" and that its approach "verged on reckless." But here's the thing about dark money operations: getting caught doesn't stop them. It just sends them back to find better data. Official government voter records are better data. That's what MAGA is collecting right now, state by state -- the raw material for a voter suppression operation that makes 2021 look like a dry run. And True the Vote doesn't operate alone. It sits inside the same vast dark money web connected to Leonard Leo -- the man who packed the Supreme Court, the man whose network has spent hundreds of millions capturing courts at every level, the man behind the system that gave Donald Trump criminal immunity. We know how this sounds. We wish it were a conspiracy theory. It isn't. This is happening in real time, in plain sight, with federal resources behind it. Here's what stops them: State Supreme Courts. Most election cases don't end up in front of Trump's hand-picked federal judges. They end up in front of state Supreme Courts -- courts whose justices are chosen by voters, not by presidents. That's why Leo's network has spent millions targeting those courts. And that's why Defend Our Courts exists. We're the counter to MAGA's sinister dark money machine that is currently trying to buy our courts and steal elections. We beat them in Pennsylvania. We beat them in Wisconsin. And now: Georgia votes on May 19th. A win in Georgia puts us on the path to flipping that court before the 2028 presidential election, before the next wave of voter suppression schemes lands in front of a judge. == | | | == | == | == | | | == | == | == | | | | == | They are building the infrastructure to steal 2028. Can I count on you to chip in now?**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/130417216/617688310/-2018920393?refcode=MW_ATA_EM_FR_EOM5_260429_T1_2&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODY1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI0NmVkMDQwNi0wNjQ0LWYxMTEtOGVmMi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=T8GYSUrhmwzOTfxdO2_ybThlR_6XO3nyaoMbK2tJFrw=)

Frankly, Derek, we can’t afford to fall behind our fundraising benchmarks. Across our Commonwealth, I am hearing from folks who are fired up to elect Democrats across Virginia – not only to hold onto this Senate seat, but flip the _four_ competitive House races for Democrats.

Okay... so I know we told you we needed to raise $7,000 by the end of the month.
That was true when I said it... But I just got out of a finance meeting with my team, and we realized we have to make some adjustments. No getting around it.
Our opponent, Diana DeGette, just put new ads up online, and after looking at the numbers, our team came to the same conclusion: we cannot keep our budget where it is and still run the campaign we need to run to win.
I wish there were a workaround. We really tried to find one, but there's no getting around it. If we want to reach enough voters, respond to what Diana is putting up, and make sure people actually hear from the candidate who doesn't take corporate PAC money, we have to expand our budget.
[So, don't hate me... but we're increasing our online goal. We now need to raise an additional $10,000 by the end of the week. Peter, MAGA was just catastrophically blown out in a deep red Louisiana special election. The 2026 Blue Tsunami is REAL & ROLLING over the blood red deep South.
I come bearing good news from the Bayou:
Louisiana is now IN PLAY. Yes, Louisiana. Let me show you how:
In deep red MAGA country that voted for Trump by 13 points, a Democrat didn't just win -- she won BIG. Defeating a diehard MAGA Republican with Trump's "total and complete" endorsement by 24 points. A 37-point over-performance.
The White House had to issue a statement saying "Don't Be a Panican. We're Winning."
My name is Jamie Davis. I'm the Democrat running for U.S. Senate in Louisiana. My family worked this land as sharecroppers, and today my son and I farm the very same fields together -- but now we own them.
Democrats have been making a desperate last stand here, and now we've broken through.
We can elect Louisiana's first Black Senator since Reconstruction.
But here's the reality: Momentum means nothing if we can't capitalize on it.
Tomorrow is our end-of-month deadline. When our numbers are finalized, the entire political world will be watching to see if this Louisiana momentum is real or a fluke.
A strong finish tomorrow shows them we're serious. It proves Louisiana isn't just in play -- it's WINNABLE.
Sounds like a lot of pressure on hitting our goals, right? Well, I won't lie to you: This is a big moment, and it's not easy for me to ask for help or people's hard-earned dollars.
But I wouldn't be asking if it wasn't crucially important to flip this seat and defeat the MAGA Extremist Machine that has a stranglehold on our state.

April 29, 2026
"Comedian" Jimmy Kimmel is in the news again. His [last foray](https://substack.com/redirect/85ce7b48-3668-47ed-959d-e5573369548c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) was when he made the following comment after the assassination of conservative speaker Charlie Kirk: "We hit some new lows over the weekend, with the MAGA gang desperately trying to characterize this kid who murdered Charlie Kirk as anything other than one of them and doing everything they can to score political points from it."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/804eb325-7bfa-4f47-86b7-70c15b5abc6a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
"Comedian" Jimmy Kimmel
Of course, the assassin, Tyler Robinson was not a MAGA acolyte but a [hardcore liberal.](https://substack.com/redirect/1b1c65c8-ffd4-4cc2-b65c-6bd7ff99d3f9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Conservatives tepidly called for Kimmel's head, but he continued his late-night show while liberals cheered him as the great defender of the First Amendment.

Kimmel, then doubled down, recently stating that the President's wife had the "glow of an expectant widow." Two days later, there was another assassination attempt on President Trump. Again, conservatives along with the President and the First Lady called for Kimmel to be removed from late night television and the FCC (Federal Communication Commission) is looking at ABC's (Kimmel's employer) license.

But Kimmel responded that he was referring to the age difference between the First Lady and the President meaning that this was the reason she would be an "expectant widow.'
| [rtenews](https://substack.com/redirect/e593a200-8ff0-4c4c-8031-1cac8f10fa8f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
---|---
[](https://substack.com/redirect/9b106ef7-d64b-4fb4-a78a-b471746aa9d5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
3,557 likes
RTÉ News on Instagram: "Jimmy Kimmel used the opening monologu...
[View on Instagram](https://substack.com/redirect/9b106ef7-d64b-4fb4-a78a-b471746aa9d5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

Of course this is a bald-faced lie. Kimmel was making a joke about a possible assassination attempt on the President. He knows it and everyone else knows it.

But the skeptical reader can watch the actual clip of Kimmel's comment below.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/06e5927d-f790-4559-97d8-76247765c2a9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

Notice the reaction of the overwhelmingly liberal crowd wildly cheering this joke. Does anyone in their right mind believe this crowd thought Kimmel's joke was funny because of the age difference between the President and First Lady? This liberal crowd was cheering at the thought of the President's assassination and Kimmel loved every minute of it.

In fact the liberal response to the recent attempt on the President's life has been typical. Some were upset that the attempt was not successful. Other liberals thought that the President staged the attempt. But the potential assassin, Cole Thomas Allen, wrote on[ social media:](https://substack.com/redirect/7dcc7d2b-6138-4eba-9b8b-f3f2bfb03709?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

"Everyone already knows Trump is a f**king awful person in multiple dimensions and no one has done sh*t,"

As part of his written manifesto justifying his assassination attempt [he wrote](https://substack.com/redirect/c2f75a74-820e-4a64-bb08-e7d9d84e10e2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg):

"And I am no longer willing to permit a pedophile, rapist, and traitor to coat my hands with his crimes."
So according to these liberals, the man who made the above statements was somehow paid off by President Trump to stage an assassination, get caught and then spend decades of time in prison. Really?
But Jimmy Kimmel has very cleverly put himself in the political position whereby his downfall causes the liberal intelligentsia to lose face. His previously political transgressions have been ignored, especially by hypocritical feminists.
Jimmy Kimmel once hosted "The Man Show" which began with large-breasted young women (called the Juggies) jumping up and down on a trampoline in wet T-shirts while Kimmel and his co-host leered.

[](https://substack.com/redirect/bafb3bc3-39ae-4bf4-97ae-6bd4ae2cc89d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

Liberal violence and assassination are now the norm. Luigi Mangione, who cowardly shot and killed US Health Care CEO Brian Thompson in the back, is a folk hero to some liberals. Violence against conservatives by liberals at our universities is routine. Liberal blogger [Hasan Piker](https://substack.com/redirect/78e296ba-161a-4b64-bf5a-e7752379db91?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), who has millions of followers, has stated the raping of Israelis in the Gaza attack was justified. He has called for the murder of Republican Florida Senator Rick Scott and mocked the assassination attempt of President Trump while cheering Kimmel on.

Former FBI Director James Comey called for President Trump's assassination by posting a picture of seashells he "supposedly" found on beach stating "86 47." ["86"](https://substack.com/redirect/312f6fa5-a118-49e2-99a1-37f32f75f44c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) is a term for killing someone while "47" refers to President Trump as he is the 47th president.

| [](https://substack.com/redirect/950e125f-05c7-493c-93b7-619678388ab0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
James Comey with the seashells he "found" on a beach.
What must be understood is that President Trump's victory was not simply an upset. It was a coup d'etat. America's ruling class was used to having compliant presidents - Republican or Democrat - bail out Wall Street, allow jobs to be shipped overseas and permit cheap labor to invade the country while having a pushover Supreme Court to do their bidding on issues such as abortion, climate change, gun control, gay rights, rigged elections etc.

President Trump changed this. As President Trump has said, "It's not me that they are after. It's you. I'm just in the way."

Thus, some members of our media and the ruling class push so-called comedians like Kimmel to enrage segments of the population to remove President Trump from office - dead or alive. Hopefully, the average person can see through this promotion of violence and thuggery and force Kimmel's employers to punish him accordingly.

With everything on the line, I’m asking you to split a donation across **six critical Senate races** that could decide who controls the chamber — plus one standout opportunity in Alaska where your dollars stretch the farthest.

Whatever you’re able to give today will be split evenly between the conservative candidates fighting in **Georgia, Maine, Michigan, North Carolina, Ohio, New Hampshire,** and in **Alaska.**

These six races are ground zero in the fight to stop the most extreme far-left Democrats running this cycle. Just take a quick glance at what we’re up against:

**Sherrod Brown in Ohio** — One of the most extreme liberals in the Democratic Party, a big-government socialist who champions higher taxes on working families, radical environmental regulations that kill jobs, and soft-on-crime policies that put Ohio families at risk. Ohio cannot afford to send this far-left ideologue back to Washington.

**Jon Ossoff in Georgia** — The vulnerable Democrat incumbent who has pushed radical immigration policies, opposed strong border security, and consistently sided with the far-left on criminal justice reform that endangers communities.

**Graham Platner in Maine** — The Bernie Sanders-backed progressive challenger with a history of extreme online rhetoric and a platform full of far-left economic populism and identity politics.

**Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan** — The leading progressive in this open Senate seat, a vocal advocate for Medicare for All, wealth redistribution, and other socialist-leaning policies that would explode taxes and government control.

**The radical Democrat ticket in North Carolina** — Democrats are targeting this open seat with candidates who have embraced defund-the-police style rhetoric and extreme positions on crime and borders — exactly what we cannot allow in the Senate.

**Chris Pappas in New Hampshire** — The leading Democrat in this open seat race has a long record of supporting far-left priorities like massive government spending, climate alarmism, and social policies that undermine traditional values. Chris Pappas is simply too liberal for the Granite State. All six of these far-left threats need to be defeated.

In Alaska, Mary Peltola is running in what could be one of the most competitive Senate races in the country. Because Alaska covers a massive 586,000 square miles — more than California, Texas, and Montana combined — reaching voters often requires expensive travel to remote communities. body:
For me as a progressive, that means making sure that we’re actually fighting for everyday people.
#
I believe in guaranteed, single-payer healthcare. We need to drive toward an America where every single person in this country can see a doctor without fear of having to choose between their insulin and their rent.
I believe in an America where we are actively transitioning out of dependency on Russian and Middle Eastern oil, and the volatility of that, so that our energy prices can be lower.
We need to be talking about universal gun safety and common-sense measures — background checks, making sure that the people most likely to kill with assault weapons don’t get those weapons, and holding people responsible who put those weapons in their hands.
**We’ve got a lot of work to do**.
For me as a progressive, having a very clear vision for that means making sure we don’t get into foreign wars that are just endless entanglements, that we’re actually fighting for everyday people, and — for the love of God — getting big money out of politics.
In solidarity,
Alexandria
We have to have a politics of integrity, not a politics of cowardice anymore.
We have to stand up for what is right in this country. **We can change the page**.
Together, we’ve built a movement fighting for critical issues — from Medicare for All to democratizing fundraising power in politics.
