clean_body: For me as a progressive, that means making sure that we’re actually fighting for everyday people. I believe in guaranteed, single-payer healthcare. We need to drive toward an America where every single person in this country can see a doctor without fear of having to choose between their insulin and their rent. I believe in an America where we are actively transitioning out of dependency on Russian and Middle Eastern oil, and the volatility of that, so that our energy prices can be lower. We need to be talking about universal gun safety and common-sense measures — background checks, making sure that the people most likely to kill with assault weapons don’t get those weapons, and holding people responsible who put those weapons in their hands. We’ve got a lot of work to do. For me as a progressive, having a very clear vision for that means making sure we don’t get into foreign wars that are just endless entanglements, that we’re actually fighting for everyday people, and — for the love of God — getting big money out of politics. In solidarity, Alexandria We have to have a politics of integrity, not a politics of cowardice anymore. We have to stand up for what is right in this country. We can change the page. Together, we’ve built a movement fighting for critical issues — from Medicare for All to democratizing fundraising power in politics. | ---|--- | | | ---|---|---|--- Email us: mailto: speak@ocasiocortez.com

name: Voting Rights Update via Dan Freeman
subject: BREAKING: What the Supreme Court did today
body:
---
| [](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-scotus-rr-april-2026?amount=7&refcode=em_20260429_6941_fr&refcode2=6941_22930333_Wvc7ZL&akid=6941%2E22930333%2EWvc7ZL)

Derek,
This is Dan Freeman, the DNC’s Litigation Director. I’m reaching out to give you an update on the Supreme Court’s decision in _Louisiana v. Callais_. I wish I had better news.
Today, the Supreme Court gutted the core requirement of the Voting Rights Act that protected majority-minority districts. This will make it _much_ harder to bring discrimination claims against redistricting maps.
The Court ignored standards set by Congress, overturned **decades** of precedent, and severely undercut a core victory of the Civil Rights Movement. With this ruling, the Court has opened the door to diluting Black, Latino, AANHPI, and Native American representation across the country, especially in the South, where Republicans have made clear they want to eliminate the voting power of minority communities.
**Derek, here’s the deal: When President Trump and his administration refuse to defend Americans’ voting rights, or actively attempt to violate them, the Democratic National Committee is ready, willing, and able to stand up and defend the American people.**
The DNC is taking on Republicans on all fronts—in the courts, in the press, on social media, and on the ground—to ensure that we elect Democrats who will stand up to these aspiring authoritarians. **This setback only strengthens our resolve to fight.**
[**If this work matters to you, please make a $7 contribution to the DNC today to help us continue bringing the fight to Trump and his allies. We will put your donation to work immediately.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-scotus-rr-april-2026?refcode=em_20260429_6941_fr&amount=7&refcode2=6941_22930333_Wvc7ZL&akid=6941%2E22930333%2EWvc7ZL)

name: Justice Democrats
subject: Why did this Democrat vote to fund ICE?
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY JUSTICE DEMOCRATS
body:
[1]Justice Democrats

Peter,

Congress is full of too many do-nothing Democrats who say one thing, then
vote the other way.

That’s especially true of Rep. Doris Matsui, who’s represented Sacramento
in Congress for over 20 years.

This year, she’s tried to take credit for opposing ICE. So why did she
vote to fund their terrorism five times? Maybe it’s because she’s taking
campaign contributions from the private contractors carrying out ICE’s
mass deportations.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260429-mv.X4XV3H&refcode=em20260429-37723&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1002&akid=37723%2E1203867%2EmgKLIh ]Tweet from @PabloReports: California Democrat Doris Matsui was born in
an internment camp. She's also voted to fund ICE five times. Now she wants
credit for opposing it. Reporting by me:'

We don’t have to settle for this kind of two-faced leadership.

That’s why we endorsed Mai Vang, who’s challenging Matsui in the CA-07
Democratic primary election on June 2.

Mai is the child of refugees, a community organizer, and a Sacramento city
councilmember who’s seen the pain Trump's fascism has caused up close.

Instead of voting to fund Trump’s American gestapo and calling to “reform”
it, Mai supports abolishing ICE.

While Matsui takes support from AIPAC, Mai supports ending military
funding to Israel.

Mai will fight for the progressive priorities we need — like Medicare for
All and the Green New Deal.

Races like this will define the future of the Democratic Party. We can be
ruled by out-of-touch, corporate-backed Democrats, or we can elect a new
generation of leaders ready to fight for the working class.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260429-mv.X4XV3H&refcode=em20260429-37723&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1003&akid=37723%2E1203867%2EmgKLIh ]Mai’s end-of-month fundraising deadline is coming up tomorrow at
midnight. Can you split a $5 grassroots donation between
her campaign and Justice Democrats to help us win in just over a month?

In each of these 26 states, the results from these Secretary of State elections will determine not just who holds those offices but how future elections are run and the shape of our democracy as a whole.
We must make sure that pro-voter, pro-democracy, anti-suppression candidates win everywhere we can. RUSH $35 or more right now to give us the resources we need to push all year to register and turn out every eligible voter >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=042926_3&amount=35]
Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
These types of elections always fly under the media's radar, Team, but this year 26 Secretary of State races will shape the future of our elections, redistricting in 2030, and the outcome of the 2028 presidential race.
Opponents of voting rights already know this, which is why they’re already pouring money into these elections – and we have to fight back now, while it still makes a difference. Check out this map:
Map of Key Secretary of State Races for 2026 [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=042926_3&amount=25]
The work to increase voter participation and turnout for these races has to start now, not this summer. We have to build the infrastructure to defend pro-voter initiatives in Arizona, Michigan, Wisconsin, and Nevada, at the same time as we work to flip the script in key battleground states like Georgia, Ohio, and Iowa.

Opponents of voting rights have been working on these objectives for years. They've targeted state legislatures and key statewide offices to control the rules around voting and that's why they've been in a position to follow up on the "Big Lie" with bill after bill suppressing the vote. They've played the long game to pick and choose their voters and protect their own power.
Most people don't know that their Secretary of State is the state official who runs their elections, let alone who the current office-holder in their state is. But they are the last line of defense against voter suppression and diminished ballot access , which is why we need to invest in voter information, registration, and participation in these critical races.
2025 was a tough year, but we did not back down. Our right to vote is too important and too much is at stake for our democracy, our fellow Americans, and the direction of our country. Driving pro-voting rights voters to the polls in November is the best possible response to all that we've been forced to live through the last decade.
Your gift -- $10, $20, $35, or more -- helps provide the resources we need to keep voters apprised of what is at stake and get them out to vote for pro-democracy policies. Please, chip in what you can today! >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=042926_3&amount=35]

Integrity First Voter Action Project is dedicated to expanding ballot access and increasing voter participation across the country.
Since the Supreme Court gutted key provisions in the Voting Rights Act, extreme politicians have taken advantage to pass harsh laws that restrict access to the ballot box. These restrictions particularly affect disadvantaged communities and people of color. It’s our goal to bring awareness to these laws wherever they may crop up and organize voters to take action to ensure the right to vote is available to everyone in their states and communities.

# [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/130421120/617700893/-349382464?refcode=em-header&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS85MDE1MyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI1MzEzMTY3Yy0wZTQ0LWYxMTEtOGVmMi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=4GKvIsLQgE6JGh8GnonnNKnPk9jOWx5ix4jHU7I5m9I=)
We'll get straight to it, Peter: Tomorrow is our end-of-month deadline, and we could really use your support with **[your first $3 donation](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/130421123/617700899/-349382464?refcode=em-4.29.26-all-a&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS85MDE1MyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI1MzEzMTY3Yy0wZTQ0LWYxMTEtOGVmMi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=4GKvIsLQgE6JGh8GnonnNKnPk9jOWx5ix4jHU7I5m9I=)**.

Before we ask you to stand with George, here are three reasons why this race is still on the map:
1. George was one of the _ONLY_ Democrats to flip a Republican-held seat in 2024. As a freshman Congressmember in the minority, it makes him a uniquely vulnerable target – and we've already seen national GOP attacks.

2. After Proposition 50 passed in California, congressional maps changed. Tens of thousands of voters – _who have never seen George's name on their ballot or know his story_ – were folded into CA-27. We need to reach them before our MAGA opponent does.

clean_body: | = Integrity first. Service before self. Excellence in all we do. I learned these values serving in the U.S. Air Force, I lived them as a nurse practitioner serving our communities, and they're exactly why I’m stepping up now. I'm Kristina Knickerbocker, and I'm running for Congress in Ohio's 10th Congressional District because our families deserve better than excuses and political theater. They deserve results. = | = I grew up in a working family where nothing came easy. I put myself through school, cared for patients in their toughest moments, and served my country in the Air Force. Now, as a mom of two, I see how the system is failing Ohio families like mine. Childcare costs more than our mortgage, and my grocery receipts from Kroger keep going up. These things aren't accidents – they're the choices of politicians in Washington who focus on partisan division and the interests of billionaires. It's time the other 99% come together to bring America's voice back to the people. I'm running for Congress because mission failure is not an option. First off, Ron DeSantis is forcing a partisan gerrymander through the Florida state legislature. Trump started this arms race, but after Democratic victories in California and Virginia, he’s more worried about control of the House than ever. Now, he’s hoping Florida might save him from facing down a Democratic Congress next year.
This might sound like bad news, but here’s our second point.
The further the GOP gerrymanders in Florida, the more risk they put their own incumbents in. DeSantis is already getting pushback from members of his own party on the maps he’s pushing. And even after they pass through the legislature, they’ve already drawn legal challenges — because partisan gerrymandering is banned under the Florida Constitution.
All that to say: This is far, far from a done deal. It’s way too early to write this off.

clean_body: As America turns 250, we must honor them while we can| | | Patriot, It's Gary Sinise here. You may know me from my roles in movies like Apollo 13 and The Green Mile or the CBS television series CSI: NY - but it was in 1994 playing the role of Lt. Dan in Forrest Gump that changed my life and inspired my enduring connection to our defenders, veterans, and first responders. I've served as an Honorary Grand Marshal for the National Memorial Day Parade in Washington, D.C. nearly every year since American Veterans Center revived it in 2005. But I've never been more excited to serve as an Honorary Grand Marshall than I am this year - the year of America's 250th birthday. Patriot, this Memorial Day marks the first major national act of remembrance of the veterans who made the ultimate sacrifice to defend America from its enemies and ensure it has remained the Land of the Free for the last 250 years. And this year's National Memorial Day Parade will be a special edition - the biggest parade yet - where national memory meets living history as veterans from every military generation celebrate America and honor the service and sacrifice of their fallen brethren. Patriot, the National Memorial Day Parade is ENIRELY FUNDED by private contributions, including from generous patriots like you. The 2026 National Memorial Day Parade is a once-in-a-lifetime moment where we need to do all we can to honor our country and our veterans. Bigger crowds. More veterans. More young people learning what courage, service, and sacrifice really mean. Historically, AVC has been able to do this at a fraction of what other major public events cost to put on each year. In fact, the entire parade costs about as much as just THREE balloons in the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade or TWO floats in the Rose Bowl Parade! That means that every dollar that's contributed by a generous American like you makes a difference for this important event. But I want to reiterate that American Veterans Center does not take ANY federal funding for this event. It is funded entirely by private citizens like you who want to honor those who have sacrificed so much for our country. | | Your support of the American Veterans Center not only helps the parade, but also supports great programs like: Record hundreds of oral histories of veterans from World War II to today before we lose these stories forever. Hold our annual American Veterans Conference, which allows young cadets a chance to hear first-hand from veterans from WWII, Korea, Vietnam, and our modern wars. Produce veteran-focused T.V. documentaries and specials that remind Americans the price of our freedom. But of course, the National Memorial Day Parade is AVC's flagship event honoring America's veterans. And this year's parade will be the largest in their history of hosting the parade. If you've been looking for an opportunity to give back to those who have given so much for our freedom, this is one of the best possible ways you could do it. And for a special group of veterans, this might be one of the last chances we get. You see, with each year that goes by, we lose more and more of our World War II veterans, and for the few we have remaining, traveling to Washington, D.C., for the parade is difficult. | | | | | WWII veterans were a key part of the first parade when it was revived in 2005, as they have been every year since for the last 20 years. But this may be the last year we have the opportunity to have these brave men and women with us for the parade. This year is a rare moment when living witnesses to World War II and America 's 250**th birthday overlap. And no matter how much you can give to this important cause, I want to ask something additional of you. On Memorial Day - not just this momentous year of military milestones, but every year - please join me in honoring those who made the ultimate sacrifice for our freedoms. Come to the National Memorial Day Parade in Washington, D.C. Visit a local veterans' cemetery. Send a note to a family of the fallen. Or simply take a quiet moment to think about the men and women who gave their lives to defend OUR country. I believe that while we can never do enough to express our gratitude to our defenders, veterans, and first responders, we can always do a little more. Patriot, thank you for your support of America 's heroes. - Sincerely, Gary Sinise Honarary Grand MarshalNational Memorial Day Parade P.S. Patriot, America is stepping into its 250th year, and this Memorial Day begins that national remembrance. Veterans across generations have given their lives to defend America and all she stands for. And for the Greatest Generation in particular, this may be the last time they're able to join us at this year's National Memorial Day Parade. There's no better send-off we can give them than to make sure they're present to honor their fallen brethren during America's 250th birthday. name: Christopher Ahuja for Congress
subject: You’re paying for Trump’s ballroom
body:
Families are barely making it

| | | | | [|
---](https://chrisahuja.us2.list-manage.com/track/click?u=67424df89870d1cac00e55f46&id=c9c4064d38&e=53c7d12fc7)
| | | | | | Peter,
When Donald Trump first announced his ballroom project, we were told it would be funded by private donors and wouldn’t fall on taxpayers.
That’s no longer the case. The $400 million price tag is now being shifted onto the public.
For families in CA-32, that isn’t an abstract number. It’s money that could be invested in lowering costs, improving schools, repairing infrastructure, or expanding access to healthcare. Instead, it’s being redirected into a project that does nothing to make life more affordable or stable for people here at home.
What’s just as troubling is the silence from Brad Sherman. This is exactly the kind of moment where our representative should be speaking out clearly against waste and demanding accountability for how taxpayer dollars are used. That leadership hasn’t shown up.
At the same time, we’re told there isn’t enough funding to address rising rent, childcare costs, or the everyday expenses stretching families thin. Those tradeoffs reflect a set of priorities, and right now they are not centered on working people in our district.
I’m running for Congress because I believe public dollars should be used to strengthen our communities, not subsidize projects like this. CA-32 deserves leadership that will actually stand up, speak out, and fight for where our money goes.
[**If you’re ready to push for that kind of accountability, I’m asking you to support this campaign with $25, $50, or $100 today.**](https://chrisahuja.us2.list-manage.com/track/click?u=67424df89870d1cac00e55f46&id=4a8f6c8205&e=53c7d12fc7)

name: David Hogg
subject: The Supreme Court strikes again
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY LEADERS WE DESERVE, LEADERSWEDESERVE
body:
SCOTUS just handed states the power to draw rigged maps designed to silence Black voters and leaders. The fight just got harder — but we aren’t backing down.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20260429-1&t=1&akid=3420%2E587540%2EIM0aAK)
Peter,
**The Supreme Court just struck a massive blow to Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act — the last major protection against racist, rigged electoral maps.**
In _Louisiana v. Callais_ , six Republican-appointed judges rewrote the rules so that proving racial discrimination in redistricting will be virtually impossible. Justice Kagan said it herself in her dissent: Section 2 is now “all but a dead letter.”
**That means states now have the power to draw rigged maps designed to silence Black communities and lock them out of political power — with no legal consequence.**
Mississippi is already calling a special session to redraw its maps. Florida is redistricting as we speak. Districts that Black communities fought for decades to win could be redrawn out of existence overnight. And this ruling opens the door for sweeping partisan gerrymandering that will decimate Black leadership and representation in Congress.
This is a moment where the work we do at Leaders We Deserve truly matters. When the courts strip away the protections that made Black representation possible, the answer isn’t to accept it. It’s to fight back even harder by putting all of our support behind bold, young Black progressive leaders who will lead with integrity and deliver the results their communities deserve, no matter who stands in their way.
Leaders We Deserve is incredibly proud to support Black progressive candidates like **Congressman Christian Menefee** , **Rep. Justin J. Pearson** , **Lauren Babb Tomlinson** , and **Donovan McKinney**. Leaders who show up every single day to fight for the communities this Court is trying to silence.
The fight just got harder. But we aren’t backing down.
**[Will you pitch in $5 today to help Leaders We Deserve continue backing the fearless leaders this moment demands?](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260429_1_vra.mz8gDB&refcode=em20260429-3420&amount=5&t=2&akid=3420%2E587540%2EIM0aAK)**

Thank you,
David Hogg

| | I'm Dave McCormick. I'm a West Point grad, combat veteran who served in the 82nd Airborne, a 7th-generation Pennsylvanian, **and I defeated an entrenched career politician in the #1 swing state of the 2024 election.**
I’ve seen firsthand what great leadership looks like. I’ve seen that even on our worst days, you have to put the needs of others first.
That’s why I made a promise to come to the Senate and work with fellow political outsiders like President Trump to shake up Washington, and I’m working to do that every single day.
Whether it’s securing the border, reducing crime in our cities, ending the fentanyl epidemic, or bringing down the cost of living–**I’m committed to delivering concrete solutions to the biggest issues we face.**
But in order to get the job done, it’s going to take all hands on deck. I need every freedom-loving American to help me shake up Washington. I promise I won't let you down.

It isn’t surprising, but that doesn’t make it any less outrageous.
The Supreme Court just ripped away another core American freedom: the right to a fair and equal vote in elections.
By allowing lawmakers to draw new voting maps that will significantly weaken representation for communities of color, the Court has just unleashed a new wave of racially discriminatory redistricting.
**Today’s ruling paves the way for Republicans to redraw maps, giving them the power to create 19 more safe GOP U.S. House seats and eliminate 191 Democratic-held state legislative seats across 10 Southern states. **
_**That’s enough to lock in one-party rule for a generation. This ruling does not just affect what state legislatures do in 2026, it has the power to affect our country’s voting maps for generations to come.**_
[**We’ve been preparing for this egregious ruling, and we’re ready to organize our pro-democracy movement against new gerrymanders. clean_body: We’ve been preparing for this. | | | | | BREAKING NEWS: In a landmark ruling, the U.S. Supreme Court opens the door for politicians to rig more voting maps in their favor by silencing Black and Brown Americans. = It isn’t surprising, but that doesn’t make it any less outrageous. The Supreme Court just ripped away another core American freedom: the right to a fair and equal vote in elections. By allowing lawmakers to draw new voting maps that will significantly weaken representation for communities of color, the Court has just unleashed a new wave of racially discriminatory redistricting. Today’s ruling paves the way for Republicans to redraw maps, giving them the power to create 19 more safe GOP U.S. House seats and eliminate 191 Democratic-held state legislative seats across 10 Southern states. That’s enough to lock in one-party rule for a generation. This ruling does not just affect what state legislatures do in 2026, it has the power to affect our country’s voting maps for generations to come. = If you've saved payment info with ActBlue Express, your donation will process automatically: = | = ---|--- = | = ---|--- = | = ---|--- Let’s be clear: this ruling, in and of itself, does not immediately redraw any maps. It does not immediately move any voters of color into new districts where their vote can’t make a difference. Those outcomes aren’t inevitable. The more we push back, the more we can limit the damage. Through grassroots mobilization, public education, coalition building, and public pressure, we can work to prevent new racially discriminatory voting maps. House Republicans just hauled in **$47 million** in a record-breaking fundraising push ahead of November's midterm elections, and it's clear why:

_They're desperate to cling to their fading majority in Congress._

They know their grip on the House is hanging by a thread, and with so much of their power on the line, they're scrambling to post massive fundraising numbers as early as possible to tout their campaign warchest.

Peter, the GOP is showing us exactly what happens when you have almost nothing real to run on, and the strategy becomes painfully obvious — raise as much money as you can and try to buy your way into power. Hey folks,
I sat down with **David Pakman** and we didn't hold back. We dug into the chaos around the White House Correspondents Dinner, the conspiracy spiral online, and what happens when we start losing our grip on reality just to score points. Then it got bigger--free speech, media pressure, and where all of this is heading. You don't want to miss this one.
**Here 's what we got into:**
* [**00:01:07**] We kick things off with the Correspondents Dinner chaos and the question everyone's asking: was any of it staged--or are people just reaching?
* [**00:04:18**] The internet conspiracy machine goes into overdrive--and why chasing clicks can warp reality faster than facts can catch up.
* [**00:06:00**] Breaking down the JD Vance moment and how security protocols actually work vs. what people think they saw.
* [**00:13:00**] Trump vs. Jimmy Kimmel escalates--and the chilling implications of a president targeting comedians and media companies.
* [**00:24:25**] The bigger picture: why independent media is in the crosshairs--and what happens if they come for platforms like this one.

This conversation is about more than one news cycle. It's about truth, power, and how easy it is to lose the thread if we're not careful. # Supreme Court strikes Louisiana racial gerrymander blow

The U.S. Supreme Court on Wednesday **[delivered a major ruling on race and redistricting,](https://substack.com/redirect/41b8105b-559e-4b1b-a2ce-578827004d3f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/41b8105b-559e-4b1b-a2ce-578827004d3f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)striking down Louisiana's second black-majority congressional district as an unconstitutional racial gerrymander.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/41b8105b-559e-4b1b-a2ce-578827004d3f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Major Constitutional Ruling:** The Supreme Court held 6-3 that Louisiana's creation of a second black-majority district was an unconstitutional racial gerrymander that placed race above all other factors.
* **Alito 's Majority Opinion:** Justice Alito wrote that Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act was designed to enforce the Constitution, not override it through race-based district drawing.
* **Kagan 's Sharp Dissent:** Justice Elena Kagan warned the decision would have far-reaching consequences and could render key portions of the Voting Rights Act all but a "dead letter."
* **Political Impact:** The ruling could significantly affect future congressional maps, with analyses suggesting between 12 and 19 Democratic seats nationwide may now be redrawn in favor of Republicans.

British police launched a large-scale dawn raid Wednesday, arresting nine members of a fringe religious group known as the Ahmadi Religion of Peace and Light **[over allegations of sexual abuse, forced marriage, and modern slavery.](https://substack.com/redirect/35b0e1c0-a03d-4e30-976d-a932c5abc547?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

---|---|---
* **Massive Dawn Operation:** Over 500 officers from multiple forces executed coordinated raids on three properties linked to the sect in Crewe, England, resulting in the arrest of nine members.
* **Serious Allegations:** The arrests stem from reports of sexual abuse, forced marriage, and modern slavery involving at least one female victim in 2023.
* **Child Welfare Concerns:** 56 homeschooled children associated with the group have been identified by police who have established welfare centers to ensure their protection during the investigation.
* **International Group:** The Ahmadi Religion of Peace and Light, founded by Abdullah Hashem, operates in about 40 countries and has faced law enforcement scrutiny in several nations beyond Britain.

We’re showing up to demand:
* Livable wages;
* Healthcare, housing, and education as guaranteed rights;
* An end to ICE terror and family separation;
* A government that works for working people, not corporations and billionaires.

Devastating news, Peter: The Supreme Court just dealt a major blow to the Voting Rights Act. The Voting Rights Act has been a pillar of American democracy since 1965 — providing critical protections that generations of Americans put their lives on the line for so that every voter, no matter their race or ZIP code, gets to have a voice in our democracy. **This ruling will have seismic effects on the ability of communities of color to be represented in the halls of power.** We are heartbroken and angry, but we aren’t wallowing in defeat. We’ve been preparing for this outcome and we aren’t wasting a single moment getting ready for the fight ahead. As you read this, Republicans in states across the country — and especially in the South — are plotting to use and misuse this ruling in efforts to throw out their maps and draw minority opportunity districts out of existence. **Let’s be clear: We can stop them, and the NDRC has a plan to fight back. We’re prepared to use every tool at our disposal — mobilizing voters, putting pressure on lawmakers, and electing fair-minded public officials — to protect the voting rights of all Americans. ** [**Rush in your emergency donation to help NDRC respond to this crisis for democracy. clean_body: This ruling is shameful. But we aren’t wallowing in defeat. We’re ready to respond. | Devastating news, Peter: The Supreme Court just dealt a major blow to the Voting Rights Act. The Voting Rights Act has been a pillar of American democracy since 1965 — providing critical protections that generations of Americans put their lives on the line for so that every voter, no matter their race or ZIP code, gets to have a voice in our democracy. This ruling will have seismic effects on the ability of communities of color to be represented in the halls of power. We are heartbroken and angry, but we aren’t wallowing in defeat. We’ve been preparing for this outcome and we aren’t wasting a single moment getting ready for the fight ahead. As you read this, Republicans in states across the country — and especially in the South — are plotting to use and misuse this ruling in efforts to throw out their maps and draw minority opportunity districts out of existence. Let’s be clear: We can stop them, and the NDRC has a plan to fight back. We’re prepared to use every tool at our disposal — mobilizing voters, putting pressure on lawmakers, and electing fair-minded public officials — to protect the voting rights of all Americans. = | If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: = | = = | = = | = As we write this, Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis is pushing through a new extreme gerrymander — saying openly that the Supreme Court has given them cover to do so. We know other Republican-held states could quickly follow suit — and the result could be a tsunami of extreme gerrymanders and district lines that attempt to silence American voters. Now that this ruling has come down, some experts believe that Republicans could redraw maps to steal more congressional seats in the months ahead. Put simply, if you thought that Donald Trump’s manufactured redistricting crisis was bad already, buckle up for what’s next. How we respond in moments like this will determine the future of our democracy and fairness in America. clean_body: | | | Peter, It's Captain Mike Bouchard. I can't thank you enough for opening this email. Now I'm asking you to give me two minutes to read the most important message you'll see today. I'm going to be honest with you upfront — I'm going to ask for a donation at the end. If you read the whole thing and still don't think even $5 can make a difference, I'll thank you for giving me the chance to make my case. My name is Captain Mike Bouchard. Bronze Star recipient. Army Paratrooper. Iraq veteran. Son of a sheriff. Grandson of a GM factory worker who spent 33 years building America's Arsenal of Democracy. I am not a career politician. I never will be. Now here's what should scare you. Michigan's 10th District is one of the radical left's TOP THREE targets in 2026. This seat is open. The last time it was open, we won by LESS THAN 1%! The Democrats know exactly what's at stake. Here's what they're already doing about it: Hakeem Jeffries, AOC, and Nancy Pelosi have already war-gamed this district They have $100 MILLION ready to destroy Republican candidates in swing seats like ours Soros-backed groups are preparing to flood this race with outside cash If they flip MI-10 and a couple others — they take the House And you know exactly what happens after that. Impeachment. Investigations. Two years of chaos. I've fought America's enemies overseas. I am not about to let them win here at home. But I need to be straight with you about something. Tonight is a BIG deadline for this campaign. What we report becomes public record. Permanent. Unchangeable. Every donor, every party leader, every political operative in Washington will look at that number and decide one of two things: If this campaign is real. Or it gets written off before the fight truly begins. I'm not someone who asks for help easily. In the Army you just figure it out. But I cannot hold this line alone — and everything is riding on tonight. It was a similar story when John James held this seat — he won by JUST UNDER 1% of the vote. I am fighting like hell to hold it and he needs you with me right now. This is your chance to send a combat veteran to Congress and stop the radical left cold. If you would rather see Pelosi and Jeffries flip MI-10 and celebrate taking back the House on national television, then I'll understand why you wouldn't donate today. Thank you for taking the time to read this. May God bless you and your family. body:
| | | Peter, when Congress says “there’s no money,” what they really mean is: not for you. **Because when it comes to tax breaks for the wealthy, endless wars, and corporate bailouts, the money somehow always shows up. That’s not a coincidence — it’s the result of deliberate choices about who this economy serves, and who it leaves behind.** And those choices are shaped in elections like a critical one coming up in less than a month. Right now, voters in Pennsylvania’s 3rd District are deciding who will represent them in Congress, and what kind of leadership they’ll get. **That’s why the Working Families Party is endorsing Chris Rabb for Congress in PA-03 — a Northwest Philly state representative who knows affordability is about whether working people can pay rent on time, afford a doctor’s visit, and earn a paycheck that actually covers the basics, and has spent years fighting to make that a reality.** [**Can you split a contribution between Chris Rabb’s campaign and WFP today? We’re working to raise as much as possible right now to fund phonebanking, textbanking, and the outreach we need to reach voters.**](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfquqxZ_WMtWQ5nsYnjR236T9a79n4BG_TYml09a7wKV07MVq0vUtylgx_daAYK7WTdYoRWQDqmc0kO4eT33kRnWYBLGvqjvK2BjIpTBcE-OgX5Vi0du548xSsq8OrERkEtVFtwm2zjNbGm3aezBtv42dIGv8T-56BY7MpYKaYGLJWjDwdEswAsQl0a_lVkgd4_e4iXWLDkNcNTpD8OI7t2VmQ4oencg7BBeXHJEYHDJtwH91Yy1eUbVIC9S7Dfd9jkw5YlFxgBIJS_8SP4QrbpwvY_UOlVcImFNhyxmBLDHLcTP4FhXmHorDQpTZRmzMX17wLwqTEZWHerJnmMXSQNUOOcf2zhksdz0aRcIW8ZR_Ow/4q7/WLgLo-DyRYGviOmecpVlsQ/h0/h001.Xmy9F7Bj1kQT2HNJw8jWUldOxXcmKlNXeZURtZZ8Nrc) [](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfquqxZ_WMtWQ5nsYnjR236T9a79n4BG_TYml09a7wKV07MVq0vUtylgx_daAYK7WTdYoRWQDqmc0kO4eT33kRnWY2RadHg0p56RHKkUJ9j21J0MeQyXVCNKK6avQqxnkS3ZmUSZLaLdSHbZcpvZTNeMPQAMn-2KHBs2tjn2LcFHJ_YpvokWYjtpyrKQfN3wxmHK92AFH8unr3faeIwQ92xjnaLihaBF9q0zCvdWAtm2GRZsb2Bepl4HasLUf_EFtgxPs5nz3QaviMPE4gb00CPO1KMULoA2b86vvxE1UeNwlqDnkovS-duKJ79xYlXGTkZ-WGEUqn3IPqgVaaRSyuXsv_fkt94UlOzpZY0xnTWDyqA/4q7/WLgLo-DyRYGviOmecpVlsQ/h1/h001.ckFFl2PfT9lGDku2BLDWpskLF0B_N3Rg_917-XluPZg) **[Donate $10 »](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfquqxZ_WMtWQ5nsYnjR236T9a79n4BG_TYml09a7wKV07MVq0vUtylgx_daAYK7WTdb99sic6uHGQtaxtSvVl7pJROUWsNo6182zablVAkZMX-cSPd7bIv0heyV5vnP44Z3tGHvhYRKotTeTYp0FBVI48e_BmChp4-LOu4ZRCPwgywFOEGrx5QRj2c_UPJ8NLYTeG2lEpOS7Kxpl-swWcpdCHLIRXRKcKoUP0NW1Nobxc6LXZg_BtC75AqoPBDKVJSl5-5M7kIo-bwjgdLOwywqYtJbhNVAhaRuhM_l9ZuFU912jZXT6B9YR7ie692CvFi611mMtLjGa2XaOXi9cmCMQLy1Qe9DUzTX7j6KucHeJ1A/4q7/WLgLo-DyRYGviOmecpVlsQ/h2/h001.XWQeu6qJkUSw6MjC737iyKbjPJCcsCC3EpnCyGiyIUk)** Chris isn’t new to this fight, Peter. He’s spent five terms in the Pennsylvania legislature representing a majority-Black, mixed-income district in Northwest Philadelphia. He’s built a record taking on corporate power, advancing policies that put people first, and standing up for his community. That’s why he's earned the support of leaders like **Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez** and **Rep. Summer Lee** — and he’s been willing to call out the influence of big money in politics, including AIPAC and outside spending in Democratic primaries. **That kind of backbone is rare, and it’s exactly what we need more of in Congress.** Because winning real change — affordable housing, healthcare without crushing debt, wages that keep up with the cost of living — requires more than just having Democrats in office. **It requires leaders who are**** _willing_****to confront the systems and interests holding it back.** This is a deep blue district, which means the winner of the May 19 Democratic primary is very likely headed to Washington. **So this race isn’t about whether a Democrat wins, Peter, it’s about what**** _kind_****.** Will it be a Working Families Party Democrat like Chris Rabb, who’s ready to take on concentrated wealth and fight for working people? Or someone who campaigns on our issues, then falls in line with corporate donors and lobbyists once they get to Congress? **We’re working to make sure it’s the first — and we’re going all in. clean_body: | | | Peter, when Congress says “there’s no money,” what they really mean is: not for you. Because when it comes to tax breaks for the wealthy, endless wars, and corporate bailouts, the money somehow always shows up. That’s not a coincidence — it’s the result of deliberate choices about who this economy serves, and who it leaves behind. And those choices are shaped in elections like a critical one coming up in less than a month. Right now, voters in Pennsylvania’s 3rd District are deciding who will represent them in Congress, and what kind of leadership they’ll get. That’s why the Working Families Party is endorsing Chris Rabb for Congress in PA-03 — a Northwest Philly state representative who knows affordability is about whether working people can pay rent on time, afford a doctor’s visit, and earn a paycheck that actually covers the basics, and has spent years fighting to make that a reality. Chris isn’t new to this fight, Peter. He’s spent five terms in the Pennsylvania legislature representing a majority-Black, mixed-income district in Northwest Philadelphia. He’s built a record taking on corporate power, advancing policies that put people first, and standing up for his community. That’s why he's earned the support of leaders like Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and Rep. Summer Lee — and he’s been willing to call out the influence of big money in politics, including AIPAC and outside spending in Democratic primaries. That kind of backbone is rare, and it’s exactly what we need more of in Congress. Because winning real change — affordable housing, healthcare without crushing debt, wages that keep up with the cost of living — requires more than just having Democrats in office. It requires leaders who are willingto confront the systems and interests holding it back. This is a deep blue district, which means the winner of the May 19 Democratic primary is very likely headed to Washington. So this race isn’t about whether a Democrat wins, Peter, it’s about what kind. Will it be a Working Families Party Democrat like Chris Rabb, who’s ready to take on concentrated wealth and fight for working people? Or someone who campaigns on our issues, then falls in line with corporate donors and lobbyists once they get to Congress? We’re working to make sure it’s the first — and we’re going all in. That means funding the organizing it takes to reach voters directly: phonebanking, textbanking, and building real relationships in the community. In solidarity, Working Families Party Thoughts? You can help find them. | | | | | | GOD'S CHILDREN ARE NOT FOR SALE | | | Friend,A little girl sat alone in the dark. Lured online by someone pretending to care and taken from her home. Kidnapped and hidden away in a remote cabin, where she was abused, and sold online. And passed from one man to another. Her name is Alice. And this is the part most people never hear. She was found. An investigator in Florida traced her trafficker's username. He saw a connection others missed and contacted the FBI. Agents followed the digital trail, tracing the trafficker's IP address. They moved in, raided the location and rescued her. Alive. Her trafficker now faces 20 years to life in prison. This is what happens when someone goes looking. This is what happens when the right tools are in place. But there are still so many children who have not been found yet. Still waiting. Still trapped. And that is why the Sound of Freedom Foundation exists. Friend, if this is your first time hearing about us, the Sound of Freedom Foundation 's mission is clear: To stop the sale of God 's children. The foundation extends the reach of the Sound of Freedom film, bringing awareness to the reality of child trafficking and taking action to stop it. Our vision is simple: A world where every child is safe and free. We work with partners to prevent exploitation before it begins, support rescue operations, and equip investigators. Our partners walk with survivors as they heal and rebuild their lives. Because rescue is only the beginning. And right now, there is an urgent need. We are launching Operation Search and Rescue, a mission to connect investigators and agents, identify traffickers, and build criminal evidence. We will support real rescue operations using tools like digital tracking and face recognition. This is how children are found and how traffickers are stopped. And today, you can be part of it. And right now, your donation will be matched, dollar for dollar.A concerned Child Defense Organization has approved a $10,000 MATCHING GRANT. You can enable the search and help the rescue mission to bring a child home. Please give as generously as you can while your gift is matched. Peter ,
Today’s Supreme Court ruling is a disaster for voting rights and fair representation.
The Court’s conservative majority struck down a majority-Black congressional district in Louisiana and weakened one of the strongest remaining tools in the Voting Rights Act, giving Republican mapmakers a clearer path to draw districts that dilute the power of Black and Brown voters.
And the people handing down this decision are not neutral guardians of democracy. They include justices like Clarence Thomas and Samuel Alito, who have faced YEARS of corruption scandals, billionaire-funded gifts, luxury travel, and glaring ethical conflicts, while still ruling on cases that determine who gets power in this country.
This ruling lands at the exact moment Donald Trump and Republican legislatures are already trying to use redistricting to protect their grip on Congress. They know their agenda is unpopular and that fair maps make it harder for them to win. So now they have a Court willing to make it easier for them to rig the rules before voters even get a say.
That is why taking back the House and Senate is so urgent.
A Democratic Congress can restore and strengthen the Voting Rights Act, investigate corruption on the Court, pass real ethics rules for justices that will lead to impeachments for violators, and stop Republicans from turning gerrymandered maps into a permanent governing strategy.
GOTV PAC is focused on the seats that can decide control of Congress. We’re helping reach the voters Republicans would rather silence, especially in the districts where turnout could be the difference between a Democratic majority and another Congress controlled by Trump’s allies.

Peter,
BREAKING: The Supreme Court just gutted the Voting Rights Act in a ruling that effectively dilutes the voting power of Black Americans.

body:
This is the reason I’m emailing you
# [](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/8?t=1&akid=1341%2E1086043%2EfZhr5r)
Peter,
I want to make sure to tell you _why_ it’s so important that folks **[step up and help us reach our $10,000 fundraising goal before our end-of-month deadline tomorrow night.](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260429-2.eGntjL&refcode=em-20260429-2&t=2&akid=1341%2E1086043%2EfZhr5r)**
Since I’ve become governor, the focus has been simple: **Work, Wages, and Wealth.**
That’s what our administration has been fighting for, for every Marylander, however we have the power to make it possible.
We’re lowering utility bills and building more housing across Maryland. We’re standing with federal workers and bringing more jobs to our state. And we’re standing up to the chaos of the federal government.
But Peter, there’s still so much more work to be done.
I’m running for re-election to keep pushing that mission of work, wages, and wealth for everybody. This campaign will only be successful if I have the support of a grassroots movement -- including you. I can’t do it alone. That’s why I’m asking:
**[Can you chip in any amount to power our movement? Anything you can give before tomorrow night’s deadline will set the pace of our re-election campaign for the summer and beyond.](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260429-2.eGntjL&refcode=em-20260429-2&t=3&akid=1341%2E1086043%2EfZhr5r)**
**[Donate $5 ››](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260429-2.eGntjL&amount=5&refcode=em-20260429-2&t=22&akid=1341%2E1086043%2EfZhr5r)**
I know that between reckless tariff policies and wars of choice overseas, the costs of the chaos coming out of Washington are being felt by our working families here at home.
I’m glad to have you by my side as we work to find solutions to bring costs down in Maryland -- and whether or not you’re able to chip in today, you’re a valuable part of our grassroots team.
Elevate,
Wes

# [The State of the Race in Michigan](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=6380051&post_id=195906736&utm_source=post-email-title&utm_campaign=email-post-title&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTk1OTA2NzM2LCJpYXQiOjE3Nzc1MDM5NzAsImV4cCI6MTc4MDA5NTk3MCwiaXNzIjoicHViLTYzODAwNTEiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.XBGK8w-Dkc0j-oon0JcG_FXgMqT2m6FRPKcd45fxoj4)
### Behind the scenes in our fight to keep Michigan blue
| | [Haley Stevens](https://substack.com/@haleyformi)
---
| Apr 29
---
| [](https://substack.com/@haleyformi)
---

---
| | | [](https://substack..Nlq8QhkIFv7WyKScL6vehbQowxdMpBYl-qXHD_V-keI?&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email)
---
| | [READ IN APP](https://open.substack.com/pub/haleyformi/p/the-state-of-the-race-in-michigan?utm_source=email&redirect=app-store&utm_campaign=email-read-in-app)
---

Friends,
I want to take a minute and give you a little behind-the-scenes look at where things stand in our battleground race here in Michigan.
When you're in the middle of a campaign, things move fast. We're traveling all over Michigan, and I'm talking to voters from everywhere. It's incredibly energizing. But I never want to lose sight of the fact that behind all of the hustle and polls and meetings, this campaign is powered by grassroots folks like you.
This is your campaign, and I want to keep you in the loop. I couldn't do any of this without you, so here's an update:
**This race is heating up.** The spotlight is getting brighter. And more money than ever is pouring into Michigan.
**One recent report from Axios projected that political ad spending in Michigan could reach $1 billion.** Take a look:
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/5c128f65-0ceb-46bd-8395-2782aac688fe?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**And Republicans have already committed $45 million in this race to back Mike Rogers through the Senate Leadership Fund** , their main Senate super PAC. This is from Michigan Public, our NPR station:
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/5c128f65-0ceb-46bd-8395-2782aac688fe?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Republicans and their MAGA megadonors know what we know: **[Michigan is a must-win for Democrats, and Senate control will run straight through this state.](https://substack.com/redirect/5c128f65-0ceb-46bd-8395-2782aac688fe?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
The good news? We're ready.
Our campaign has real momentum. **Just this week, a poll - the ninth overall - came out showing us ahead of our primary opponents. **That's huge.
It tells me people are hearing our message, and they believe me when I say I'm going to fight harder than anyone for them in the U.S. Senate. Michiganders can tell I mean it when I talk about lowering costs, creating jobs, and making government work for working people.
That's part of the reason I've **earned more union endorsements than any other candidate in this race.**
I'm so proud of that.
Because when the people who actually do the work - on the shop floor, on the job site, and in our union halls - decide to stand with you, that says something.
It's about trust. Showing up. Listening. Doing the work. Delivering results.
**These good polling numbers and this union support didn 't magically appear. They came from years of fighting for manufacturing, standing up for workers, helping lead the auto rescue, and pushing to bring jobs and investment back to Michigan.**
So yes, this race is getting more competitive and more expensive by the day.
Yes, the outside money is real.
Yes, the MAGA megadonors are coming.
But yes, our momentum is real too.
This people-powered campaign is made up of teachers and nurses, autoworkers, small-business owners, parents, and retirees who care deeply about this state and who are tired of billionaires and dark money trying to drown us out.
**[I'm so proud to be in this fight with each and every one of you.](https://substack.com/redirect/5c128f65-0ceb-46bd-8395-2782aac688fe?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
If you're in a position to chip in, I'd be grateful. Truly. Even giving a few dollars helps us keep building this campaign the right way. And we've got a big end-of-month deadline coming up on Thursday at midnight, so any amount would be deeply appreciated.

subject: Judicial Watch Lawsuit Settlement Causes Review and Removal of 800,000 Ineligible Voters from Oregon Voter Rolls
body:
Judicial Watch announced a settlement in its federal lawsuit against
Oregon election officials, which confirms 800,000 ineligible voter
names are slated for review and removal from voter registration lists.
The settlement requires state officials to produce detailed data and
enforce federal voter roll clean-up procedures under the National
Voter Registration Act of 1993 (NVRA).

Meet Coach Tuberville:

**Coach Tuberville was born in Camden, Arkansas, the third of three children of Olive and Charles Tuberville. College Football 's 2004 Coach of the Year and two-time SEC Coach of the Year, Tommy Tuberville is most often recognized for his success on the field. But it is the legacy of his father, a highly decorated WWII veteran and Purple Heart recipient, that motivates Coach Tuberville to give back to the brave men and women of the United States Armed Forces.

In 1989 Coach Tuberville met his future wife, Suzanne Fette, at the Sugar Bowl in New Orleans. They were married in 1991 and have two boys, Tucker and Troy, who continue to make their dad proud.

In his career as a College Football Coach, Tommy started a long and successful career at the University of Miami, starting as a graduate assistant and rising to the Hurricanes' defensive coordinator. He led the Canes to three AP national championships and coached future Hall of Famers Ray Lewis and Warren Sapp, as well as Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson.

In 1998, Coach Tuberville was announced as the next head coach for the Auburn Tigers. Tuberville's time at Auburn was a success by any measure, as the Tigers captured eight consecutive bowl appearances, including five New Year's Day bowl appearances, five SEC Western Division titles, one SEC Championship, and a 13-0 season in 2004, after which Coach Tuberville was once again named the AP's SEC Coach of the Year. For his efforts during the perfect 2004 season, Tuberville would be named Paul "Bear" Bryant Coach of the Year, Associated Press Coach of the Year, Walter Camp Coach of the Year, Sporting News Coach of the Year, and AFCA Coach of the Year, among others.

_In 2020, Coach Tuberville became Senator Tuberville, winning his election to represent all Alabamians in the United States Senate with the full support of President Trump. Since then, he's supported President Trump's America-First policies while fighting off the Radical Left. For America, Coach Tuberville Meet Coach Tuberville: Coach Tuberville was born in Camden, Arkansas, the third of three children of Olive and Charles Tuberville. College Football 's 2004 Coach of the Year and two-time SEC Coach of the Year, Tommy Tuberville is most often recognized for his success on the field. But it is the legacy of his father, a highly decorated WWII veteran and Purple Heart recipient, that motivates Coach Tuberville to give back to the brave men and women of the United States Armed Forces. In 1989 Coach Tuberville met his future wife, Suzanne Fette, at the Sugar Bowl in New Orleans. They were married in 1991 and have two boys, Tucker and Troy, who continue to make their dad proud. In his career as a College Football Coach, Tommy started a long and successful career at the University of Miami, starting as a graduate assistant and rising to the Hurricanes' defensive coordinator. He led the Canes to three AP national championships and coached future Hall of Famers Ray Lewis and Warren Sapp, as well as Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson. In 1998, Coach Tuberville was announced as the next head coach for the Auburn Tigers. Tuberville's time at Auburn was a success by any measure, as the Tigers captured eight consecutive bowl appearances, including five New Year's Day bowl appearances, five SEC Western Division titles, one SEC Championship, and a 13-0 season in 2004, after which Coach Tuberville was once again named the AP's SEC Coach of the Year. For his efforts during the perfect 2004 season, Tuberville would be named Paul "Bear" Bryant Coach of the Year, Associated Press Coach of the Year, Walter Camp Coach of the Year, Sporting News Coach of the Year, and AFCA Coach of the Year, among others. In 2020, Coach Tuberville became Senator Tuberville, winning his election to represent all Alabamians in the United States Senate with the full support of President Trump. Since then, he's supported President Trump's America-First policies while fighting off the Radical Left. In his first term as Senator, Tommy was one of eight Republicans to vote against certifying the 2020 election, has been a strong pro-life advocate, and called out Democrats for being pro-crime. SCOTUS Strikes Down Racial Gerrymander

The Supreme Court [struck down](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyc0LFu7CAQheGnwZ1XMIvNUlDcxt3eNqWFh7GNgsGC8eb1o03eIPUnnSP9H8_56WOKefvvD3KV1zmUMC_lWNpOKTUsFwfC2GLJjfIMEsZe6h7snNOsuuACBq-wI6eMMYPUVt-73Y2o7IqEIagFH8Eaq9Gq4MnCaqUcu-jeU1KDhTsAqNtjGCVpo8wCi0QdhJY-UeVbpfNaUkSf2bfPtVSkG5ajS25nPpu4_xMwCZh4pz2m9DYBU6XtSp5jyQImLFflfvHMiZqAaXgM2hjZt-usdFD_66_CMW99jdvOrffIAqauunB-xZRiG43Qcjt8_Lno-A-1Xg6-AwAA__-ZtXq6) Louisiana's race-based congressional map Wednesday in a 6-3 decision conservatives hailed as a long-overdue rebuke to race-conscious redistricting. Justice Samuel Alito's majority opinion declared that "allowing race to play any part in government decisionmaking" departs from constitutional norms applied in nearly every other context. Lower courts had [forced Louisiana](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckL1urDAQhZ_GdF6ZwctP4eI2dHvblGiwZ2GUASPbbJS3j9giD5BupPn0naPz8ZgeyML78h83cqk8pxDDNMdtziuJZB_PEshz5rhn2icw0GpjNQzTLlNdBRd8wNpX5Oqu6-7GDrapVjf3BvoOTW371jSN96EJoe5hIML5PgwVu0tlLAzQAEB96--tIdvV3Qyz8TYoa1AolVui45yFPe4F8-czJk83H7dK3FrKkVXzT8GoYAzI8u1RhNL1VzBeCQpGY697UDDm80i0kfbxTEW_YuF90YmXtWj0RUs8OTPuqF_6EiFnnShwLon9m_0lFIxVcuH4YhHObaesWTZkeTcrfxjy5eAnAAD__6kjg1o) to draw a second majority-Black district under Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act, which the high court invalidated as a violation of the Fourteenth Amendment. The decision could carry [major implications](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyc0D-vpCAUBfBPgx0G7-AgBcU2drPtloY_V70ZBAO47sffzCtf-erfycnJ-fNaXpYipe23PdCUti4hh8Xlw9UdY6w-Xy2gp0o5VUwLCHhyITnoJcVl6IIJPtjBd2gGpdQopJaPbjchAE6gtZ3WdZKr06sa9eSdk-OoYQwdmU-VkKDhAQBDP41PgVINyoETXgYmhY1YWl_wvFwkb1Oz9b3m4rH3-eii2Vs7K3v8YjAzmO_77m9bd0pbywn_2YMSlk-UwZzwrgzmep0FD-Q-X6UxmKUchFTiu_DaCr2x8pDvxIv1yJ2tGHjBQB_zjdLGD3tySjzmiyrZZBnMXTHhvClGqk_FpNgOS_FrbvvBu38N_A8AAP__wYyM1w) for the 2026 midterms, freeing GOP-led states from race-conscious mandates and reshaping redistricting nationwide. ★★★
House GOP in Meltdown

Speaker Mike Johnson is pushing FISA Section 702 renewal, the farm bill, and the Senate-passed DHS reconciliation bill through the House before recess -- and [conservatives are revolting](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyc0DFu9CAUBODT4A4LP4P5KSj-xt2mTWlheLsmi8HisescP3KOkG6kkb6R5vO23FxMMT8-3I62tvsSSljWsq-0YUrky6sF9JFiyYR5AQETF5KDWXJahi7Y4IMbfId20ForIY0cu80ar1EpHJUZYZyCB4VCC6F9UNqsCF20FyUkGBgBYOj_qUmg1INeYRVeBiaFS1hbX_F4rSl6l5uj571Uj70ve5fs1tpBbPzPYGYwn-fZu-9Y6GoZzJfPYBbyyobBvMcn8q-yZSqZP8rBK75LajxsxGl7tVDOzO-RXFdtOM6YUqRJMykeu4vpd7P94aK3hZ8AAAD__52KdLc). The jammed agenda has exposed just how thin Johnson's margin is heading into the break. The DHS shutdown is now 72 days old, with Secret Service and TSA workers at risk of going unpaid. Senate Republicans and White House budget officials are pressing the House to pass the Senate bill as written, but Johnson says it needs modifications -- a standoff that [The Hill has detailed](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckL2O5CAQBp8GMkbQBv8EBJc4m0svtPhpG3QYLINntG-_Giebb1ZSS6Xq799zeZqYYt7-mh312dbFF7_YstsaMKXqytU8ulhjyRXzAhx6xiWDaclpEdRr77wRjqIWwzAoLifZ0aBVD51duULfj84Amm7sLYIUYrTGjo5G_VFxCRN0ACAeo-o5ykEMFix30hPJTcKzPU48LpuiM7mZ-n8tp8OHKztNOrR2VNL9ITATmFvAEFP63AjMoeyY8V1vvCoSmNWoxKQk28rBGub7JRbzjesXKy88mQ-VrVf2MW_MYnsjZlYxm4bs1rCfmo-antof75hSrP1AJN92E-8C2n4x5kvDdwAAAP__II-GaQ). White House budget officials sent a memo urging immediate passage of the Senate DHS bill, warning of operational consequences from the ongoing shutdown. Johnson's insistence on modifications [sends it back to the Senate](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyc0LFuhiAUBeCnwQ2DV36RgaGL29-1owEu6k0RjGB9_cY-QreTnOTLyfl6z29LkdL6afdgzrrMmHF2eXdlCzEWn6-KwVOhnEpIMwgYuJAc9Jzi3DVo0KPtfBNMp5R6Call32zG65dGPWAv-kEuYhy0CCr06J1aRqGwIfNQQoKGHgC6dnwNIkjVKQdOeIlMChvDWdszHJeL5G2qtnwv-fSh9XlvotlqPQrrPxhMDKb7vluf0tMxmB6dwSTkk0cG05EjVfKFwYRb4WW7KuY78Xpe-8HdhWuoPC8LebKx8C1fJfA1H81p8LgpRiqDYlKsu6X4N6D-468fA78BAAD__-cAebc) -- making pre-recess passage nearly impossible. ★★★
WHCA Suspect Update

Cole Tomas Allen, 31, faces federal charges for allegedly attempting to assassinate President Trump at the White House Correspondents' Dinner on April 25. DOJ unsealed the charges on April 27. Allen, a California engineer, had [no prior extremist footprint](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckL2O6yAUhJ_G7rDgQCApKG6TLrfd0uLnOD5aDBaQeB9_5TzClqNPmtF8X4_54ShRfv53G9ralzmWOPuy-bZiSi2UV48YqFHJDfMMHDTjisFtzmkWY7QxRCfCiFYYYy5c3ZQcV-uvSjsjtPEmihAiN9KhWpSUmkt0fiR7VnEFN5AAIKbrRXNURhgPngcVB8VdwtqnivvLJwoud9e-l1IDTqFsY7Jr73sb5L8B7gPcj-OYlvKT8WgnH-Ce6I3szCddqSNby6shC6VWbHvJEXNvLFLOWFlbS-mUn597hoEeq437QSlR02ZQ_Lk5Sp_p_gdTbwu_AQAA__-csXmF) -- an outlier by every conventional threat profile. Allen left a note telling family it was his "duty" to target Trump administration officials. [New NPR reporting](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyc0LGSrCAQheGnwQwLWxQNCG5iNjfd0ELoUWqxsWhm3cffmn2EzU701an_47E-XEyR9v_uRFvqcw05rFs-Nz4wJfb5VQP6yDETI62gYJRKS5hXSmvXBBt8cJ1v0HbGmEHpWffNYb16zgYnMPMWZgODU6PzMLpNGzQj9k20b0ppmKEHgK6dhlGhNp3ZYFNeB6GVS1hqW_B6bSl6R9Xx5zMXj63PZ5PsUevFov8nYBGw3Pfd0lXaXHYBy1sXsCj93pOAhb4ld3KYVKdHI2DxOaF0KSFJfvGFvsrb8RFpr5mkz6UgX5kCUmUZIhEWyUfONdLeFBuuO6YUeTRCq_10Mf2eqn9o-GXhJwAA__856IA2) explores what drove a seemingly apolitical individual toward attempted political assassination -- a question investigators and journalists are still working to answer. The case has prompted a broader conversation about lone-actor political violence and whether existing threat assessment frameworks missed warning signs. Allen remains in federal custody as [prosecutors build their case](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckLGOpDAQRL_GZCDTNuMhcHAJ2Vx6ITLuZmidsZFtBu3fr9hP2KykKtWT3r_X_HIcOL7_up1sruuMCecl7UvZKITi01mRPBdOsVCcQcKjlbqFcY5h7hu06NH1viHbG2MGqUetms0qpZVanRs84NPjitLp0eAAThnQTjVs7yupYQQFAH33HB6StOnNAov0GoWWLlCuXabjXAJ7F6sr_9eUPXU-7U2wW61HEeqPgEnAdF1XF78q71TuXsAU-EMCphskYJL6zkbAdJZ7vnGldktnoRY5Rsptzed-tGVLqXJ8N9nicXEIXB5GaPneHYcfcv2FqI-F7wAAAP__z_x3DQ), with legal proceedings expected to unfold over months.

Craig Enters MN Senate Race

Rep. Angie Craig entered Minnesota's open Senate race, joining Lt. Gov. Peggy Flanagan -- Sanders-endorsed -- in the Democratic primary. Craig's moderate appeal gives Democrats their best electability argument in a seat [Republicans can win with the wrong nominee](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyc0LGO6yAQheGnwV0sPCYmKShu4y633RIBM45HOwbLkPXrr5JH2PpIn47-r4d_BBbOz_9hI3e0xWNBH8sW60oiNZVXQ0pcueRK2YOG6aLNBe4-ix86dJgwDKkjN1hrr9rczditDpMNt2lECjRM0ZKFeI0II6LWyxJ1x-5NaQN3GAFg6G_XSZOxg40QdTKojA5CR-sP2l9ROIXcQv1eypGoT2XrxK2t7VWN_xTMCubzPPscU6azvncF816EG6eqYP78JqHUuOTucLifLMJ1ssro5xZYPmb7Q4IfB78BAAD__1TPa6c).

[Democrats couldn't script a better midterm message than this](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyc0DFuxCAUBNDT4A7r8xfDuqBI427TprQwfK9RMFiA4-tHzhHSTTGaJ83Xa37ZEEN6f9qdTGnr7LOfl7wvdaMYq8tn8-RCDTlVSjMCKg6S4zinOIvOG--8Fa4jI7TWA8hRPrrNANE6iAUEkVJipFWDQie0ICeU1GsXzD0FEkd8IKLon4MCklroBRdw0jMJNlJpfaHjXGJwNjVbv9dcHPUu7100W2tHZY8PhhPD6bqu_sgxtODyXWA4Jboqw-mWGE4g7_xkOPmcbPS8lXM_-JbPSvydD75TrRzgOWqNQ1eMP64QY6hKMwnv3Yb4B7d__PRj8DcAAP__v811Ag).

[Secret Service and TSA workers face missed paychecks.](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyc0LGOpDAMxvGnCZ1RMAGGIsU1dHPtlSgkZogmJCgOh2affsU-wnaWftJf1vfvOT-NDz6-_pqddC7r7JKbl7QvvFEIbNNZHFnPPkWmOKPEHqQCHOcY5qZy2llnGluRboZh6KQaVVtt2j3Gtl07SWokXJe1bx5uVNjJzlm79G3l9Z2SCkdsEbGpH10vSQ3NsOAirXJCSRMolzrTcS7BWxOL4feasqXapr0KeivlYNH-ETgJnK7rqi82XzcKnO68wEmq-x5v33wh2NLJBGw-DOsZHcNhPlDYQCobZdjSTsFEB0z2zL584Er5TZnh8iEApxQhnxHSWQROVdbuuMFzPwglX7vx4ee58ost_2v8DgAA__9ZsoR3)

Section 702 of FISA -- the intelligence community's primary foreign surveillance authority -- faces expiration amid House chaos. Johnson is trying to attach a long-term renewal to the pre-recess package, but [hardliners oppose it on privacy grounds.](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyc0DFu9CAUBODT4A4LP4P5KSj-xt2mTWlheLsmi8HisescP3KOkG6kkb6R5vO23FxMMT8-3I62tvsSSljWsq-0YUrky6sF9JFiyYR5AQETF5KDWXJahi7Y4IMbfId20ForIY0cu80ar1EpHJUZYZyCB4VCC6F9UNqsCF20FyUkGBgBYOj_qUmg1INeYRVeBiaFS1hbX_F4rSl6l5uj571Uj70ve5fs1tpBbPzPYGYwn-fZu-9Y6GoZzJfPYBbyyobBvMcn8q-yZSqZP8rBK75LajxsxGl7tVDOzO-RXFdtOM6YUqRJMykeu4vpd7P94aK3hZ8AAAD__52KdLc)

subject: What we need to do:
body:

Derek, In case you haven’t heard, the Supreme Court just decided _Louisiana v. Callais_ , gutting the last truly enforceable tenets of the Voting Rights Act protecting majority-minority districts. This decision comes hand-in-hand with Trump and his Republican allies’ mission to weaken the voting power of communities of color across the country. [**If you’re as fired up as we are, you can chip in here to fund our voter protection work.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-scotus-rr-april-2026?amount=7&refcode=em_20260429_6944_fr&refcode2=6944_22930333_P47Ppd&akid=6944%2E22930333%2EP47Ppd) This is a devastating gut-punch to Americans and voters of color everywhere, but Democrats are determined to fight tooth and nail to ensure the voices of _all_ Americans are heard in November and every election that follows. **Here’s our path forward:** The DNC is already working overtime on the ground in key battleground states to register hundreds of thousands of new Democratic voters ahead of November’s midterms. We’re building power in our state parties and investing nationwide to ensure they have the resources they need to win down-ballot elections this year and beyond. **_And we’re organizing across the country to reach as many voters as possible, because we must win back Congress this year._** Here’s the truth, Derek: We know this is a dark moment in our history, but by winning back Congress this year and beginning to work to win back the White House in 2028, Democrats have the ability to mitigate the harm this decision could (and likely will) cause in the upcoming years. And by putting a Democrat in the White House two years from now, we have the chance to change the balance of the Supreme Court with justices who believe in and will protect the voting rights of Americans of color everywhere. This is God multiplying love. Jesus said, " Whoever welcomes one little child like this in my name welcomes me." (Matthew 18:5) Today you can be that welcome. You can enable the search and help the rescue mission to bring a child home. Please give as generously as you can while your gift is matched.
